Based on the novel by Laura Dave , who developed the show with Josh Singer, The Last Thing He Told Me centers on Hannah Hall (Jennifer Garner) and her young stepdaughter after the mysterious disappearance of her husband. Debuting in April 2023 and consisting of seven episodes, the adaptation made a splash upon its premiere. It became Apple's most-watched limited series since the streaming service's debut in 2019, speeding up talks for The Last Thing He Told Me season 2. Apple reveals that The Last Thing He Told Me season 2 will premiere on Friday, February 20, 2026, and will consist of eight episodes. The photos, included below, reveal Garner's reunion with her 13 Going on 30 co-star Judy Greer. Based on the upcoming novel The First Time I Saw Him by Laura Dave, the upcoming episodes pick up as Hannah's husband, Owen (Nikolaj Coster-Waldau), returns after five years on the run. Hannah (Garner) and her stepdaughter Bailey (Angourie Rice) find themselves in a race, needing to figure out how to reunite their family before the past catches up to them. This picks up after the season 1 ending, which reveals that Owen is alive but in hiding. Along with Garner, Coster-Waldau, Rice, and Greer, The Last Thing He Told Me season 2 cast includes David Morse, Augusto Aguilera, Josh Hamilton, Nick Hargrove, Michael Galante, John Noble, Michael Hyatt, Luke Kirby, and Rita Wilson. Notable supporting actors from season 1, such as Criminal Minds star Aisha Tyler, are not mentioned, but they could potentially be making guest appearances. The Last Thing He Told Me is produced by 20th Television and Hello Sunshine, a part of Candle Media. It's executive produced by Dave, Singer, and Garner, as well as Hello Sunshine’s Reese Witherspoon and Lauren Neustadter. Daisy von Scherler Mayer and Merri D. Howard also serve as executive producers alongside new co-showrunner Aaron Zelman. The next chapter in the saga of the Apple TV series, which sees Garner returning as executive producer, will have to contend with a promise Owen made to stay away from Bailey. That is potentially complicated by his direct encounter with Hannah. But it'll also have to deal with making the jump from limited series to ongoing drama. The Last Thing He Told Me season 1 made some book changes to better fit the screen. It will have to make some more adjustments, with the hope that Hannah's story is one that viewers will still be invested in after a break of almost three years. Based on the talent involved, the interest will likely still be there even after the hiatus. Dogs, however, have routinely gotten the short end of the bone. It's all werewolves and Cujo , the Stephen King story about a rabid dog. Thankfully, Good Boy is changing that, and you can watch it this month on Shudder. (And no, we're not talking about the 2020 Blumhouse/Hulu movie starring Judy Greer , though that's also fun.) Good Boy hails from IFC Films and pits a hero dog against the ghosts haunting the home where he (Indy) and his human (Todd) live. The film's synopsis explains that after moving into a new house, "Indy is immediately vexed by empty corners, tracks an invisible presence only he can see, perceives phantasmagoric warnings from a long-dead dog, and is haunted by visions of the previous occupant’s grim death." Then, when Todd starts losing himself to the evil in his house, it's up to Indy to save the day. Photo: Danielle Freiberg/IFC Films Of course, the movie is about much more than a dog taking on a haunted house. Director Ben Leonberg spoke with Polygon about the film and how and why it ends the way it does. He summed the story up thusly: "[ Good Boy ] just imagines the shoe being on the other foot. What would it be like for a dog who is sensing an ever-growing, closer and closer, invisible, dark force? What would that story be like for them?" In addition to directing Good Boy , Leonberg also produces with his wife, Kari Fischer. The real star, though, Indy, is merely playing himself. He's actually Leonberg and Fischer's own dog, which might technically make him a nepo puppy. Per a press release that rightly chose to focus on the dog, Indy "is a middle-aged, 35-pound retriever who has no idea that he’s a movie star...or does he? His favorite things are fetch, food, and his humans, Ben & Kari — in that order." He's also good at finding tennis balls and staring you down until you feed him dinner. Typical Hollywood behavior, if you ask us. Good Boy had a short theatrical run in October, earning over $8 million on a budget of only $70,000. It was also well received critically, with a 90% Fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes . Now Good Boy comes to Shudder on Nov. 21, just in time to sit down and watch it with the family for Thanksgiving. Who needs the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade when we can watch Indy save the day? Correction (Nov. 13): A previous version of this article misstated the budget for Good Boy. What's most interesting about this choice is that all of them, including main players Cooper Hoffman and David Jonsson , will be campaigning in the supporting acting categories across all the major awards circuits. This report comes exclusively from Variety , and its news that comes as surprising, but understandable. Overall, it's due to the magnitude of the film's story and how much it was reliant on the ensemble entirely rather than one actor. The Long Walk was released in September and was adapted by screenwriter JT Mollner from the novel of the same name written by Stephen King . The movie centers around teens who take part in a deadly contest where they have to keep walking or be shot on sight by the military if they fall under a certain speed. The movie was directed by Francis Lawrence, who is best known for directing several movies in The Hunger Games series of films. His transition to Stephen King's dystopian world was a huge success, with the film earning an 88% certified fresh rating on the review aggregate website Rotten Tomatoes. Part of what made The Long Walk such a successful film in the first place (and more than likely why Lionsgate is taking its interesting approach to awards season) is the chemistry between all the actors . While Hoffman and Jonsson are undeniably at the heart of the story, each individual character gets a moment to shine. The camaraderie among the walkers in the face of inevitable death is why The Long Walk is such a moving film. In 'The Long Walk,' Every Cast Member is Essential Lionsgate Variety's report states that the creative team behind the film is firm in their belief that the premise and emotional investment hinges on every single actor working in unison . So, it only makes sense that all the main actors in the film, which includes the likes of Ben Wang, Garrett Wareing, Charlie Plummer, Tut Nyuot Jordan Gonzalez, and Joshua Odjick, will have a chance to be nominated. This plan will be reflected in any potential nominations at the Oscars, Golden Globes, Screen Actors Guild Awards, BAFTA, and the Independent Spirit Awards. The report also mentions that Judy Greer, who plays Hoffman's mother in the movie, will also be put forward in the supporting actress category of the aforementioned award ceremonies. 2025 has been a phenomenal year for Stephen King adaptations, with The Life of Chuck and The Running Man also being released this year. Each director behind the three King adaptations this year has brought their own distinct style to the stories, and The Long Walk stands out thanks to its brutality and timeliness. It will be interesting to see if any unexpected cast members get nominated for their work on the film outside of favorites like Hoffman or Jonsson. One aspect that will undoubtedly stand out is the final moments of several of the characters, as each actor brought raw emotion and intensity that made the stakes feel real. For a half century now, the author has found his novels and short stories adapted for both the big and small screen. 50 years is a long time, and they have shown great advances in the craft of filmmaking, but what remains steady is how adaptations have well-drawn characters to work with. How convincingly the projects are able to bring the stories’ supernatural elements to life is secondary to them. But, with the release of Edgar Wright’s The Running Man , the second adaptation of King’s 1982 novel, there has never been a better time to ask, “Can second cinematic takes on a King novel work better than the first time?” As one might expect, the results have varied. Videos by ComicBook.com What follows are the five big screen movies that were the second attempt to bring a King work to life. The film could have been a remake of a miniseries, but the remake must have gone to theaters. For instance, Salem’s Lot (2024) didn’t count because it debuted on HBO Max. How does The Running Man stack up against its sophomore effort brethren? Let’s find out. 5) Firestarter image courtesy of universal pictures Keith Thomas’ 2022 version of Firestarter was widely deemed inferior to the 1984 original, which wasn’t even a remotely high bar to clear. But that consensus is fair, as it’s a bland and not particularly visually appealing remake. Of all the more modern Stephen King movies, Firestarter feels the most loss. Everyone involved seems to know they’re in a wholly generic work and none of them seem to be giving it their all. The Razzie nomination for young Ryan Kiera Armstrong was out of line , but this is definitely a movie worthy of receiving some not so desirable Razzie love. Stream Firestarter on Netflix. 4) Carrie image courtesy of sony pictures releasing Unlike Firestarter , Carrie (2013) did have a high bar to clear in Brian De Palma’s 1976 classic, the very first cinematic adaptation of King’s works. And, while it does fall short in every regard, there are worse things Carrie could have been than wholly average. Chloë Grace Moretz tries, but she seems a bit miscast. Then there’s Julianne Moore, who overacts not unlike Piper Laurie did in De Palma’s film, but that was a particular tightrope Laurie walked to a much more successful degree. For the most part the movie just seems to exist to cash in on a brand name and make some swift and easy money for Sony on a relatively low-risk $30 million budget. All that said, it does have two performances that rival the work seen in the original film. Namely, Judy Greer was a great choice for the empathic Ms. Desjardin and Portia Doubleday is note perfect as the bullying Chris Hargensen. They steal the movie, but that’s not enough to make it good when most of the runtime is, of course, devoted to Carrie and Margaret White. Stream Carrie on fuboTV. Read Next The 10 Best Stephen King Adaptations by His Frequent Directors 3) Pet Sematary image courtesy of paramount pictures Technically, the 2019 version of Pet Sematary is better than Mary Lambert’s 1989 take . That film, which has a strong reputation it doesn’t quite deserve, is both self-serious and an utter cheese fest. It has what is undoubtedly the best screamed to the heavens “No!” in film history, including Darth Vader’s. The thing is, between the cheese of the screenplay and the charming performance by Fred Gwynne, the 1989 Pet Sematary is memorable. The 2019 version? It’s just dour and bland. That said, it is well-cast, with both Jason Clarke and Amy Seimetz struggling to inject some life into a film that seems to be trying to capitalize on It ‘s success two years prior. Stream Pet Sematary on Paramount+. 2) The Running Man image courtesy of paramount pictures Thanks to a charismatic lead performance by Glen Powell and typically stylish direction by Edgar Wright, The Running Man manages to stand above the 1987 Arnold Schwarzenegger fronted version even if it will likely escape the viewer’s memory shortly after the credits have rolled. Much to its credit it doesn’t take long to get going and, once it starts, it never stops. It’s a perfectly suitable and digestible popcorn movie, one that never quite goes as far as it should in its commentary about modern day society but gets points for trying, nonetheless. Perhaps most importantly, this is further proof after Anyone But You , Hit Man , and Twisters that Powell has exactly what it takes to carry a movie. 1) It & It Chapter Two image courtesy of warner bros. pictures As mentioned, we’re including movies that are more modernized versions of miniseries. However, it would be fair to debate just how much of an influence Tommy Lee Wallace’s 1990 It miniseries was on Andy Muschietti’s big screen duology. If anything, it was more inspired by another cinematic adaptation of King’s works: Stand by Me . Muschietti has stated that he wasn’t a big fan of the miniseries but, even still, that miniseries (which is structurally non-chronological, just like King’s book) existed before It and It Chapter Two , so we’re including them. And, while It Chapter Two is a major step down from its predecessor, it’s still good enough to help the duology secure the number one spot. Directed by Dallas Jenkins (the multi-hyphenate filmmaker behind the TV series The Chosen ), this funny and moving film was released theatrically in November 2024. Lionsgate is releasing a Blu-ray/DVD/Digital HD combo pack just in time for this year’s festivities. The story centers on two families. Matriarch of the comfortably middle-class Bradley family, Grace (Judy Greer), has volunteered to direct their town church’s annual Christmas pageant. The woman usually in charge is sidelined due to injury. Grace and her husband Bob (Pete Holmes), along with their children Beth (Molly Belle Wright) and Charlie (Sebastian Billingsley-Rodriguez), aren’t nearly as judgmental as many of the families who attend their church. In fact, some of the other mothers believe Grace isn’t up to the task of spearheading the production. Things only become more contentious when the six Herdman kids, hellions who don’t normally attend church, decide to attend Sunday school (for the free snacks). Upon learning about the upcoming pageant, the six unruly Herdmans sign up for parts. The eldest, Imogene (Beatrice Schneider), wants to portray Mother Mary. Most of the snooty parishioners urge Grace to bar the Herdmans, universally considered to be the town hooligans (their parents remain unseen throughout), from participation. Even openminded Beth (who, in adult form—voiced by Lauren Graham—narrates the picture) is initially skeptical about the Herdmans’ ability to behave appropriately. The class struggle, middle versus lower, is central to this tale. Turns out Bob knows where the Herdman kids live as he has been delivering a Christmas ham to their residence for years. Taken aback by this revelation, and dismayed by their living conditions, Grace begins to believe in the Herdman kids’ apparent convictions. Imogene convinces her siblings to conduct deep research into the Christmas story to hopefully inject some gritty realism into the pageant. To reveal much more would risk spoiling the film’s considerable charms. Suffice it to say, things unfold in a far more nuanced way than one might suspect of a crowd-pleasing holiday comedy. It’s more of a drama, and the efforts by both families (the Bradleys’ growing realization that goodness and virtue exist outside of the bourgeoisie; the Herdmans’ discovery of a sense of personal pride) provide a genuine heart and soul to what could’ve easily been a silly romp. Have the tissues nearby (but also know, this isn’t a tragedy). Lionsgate’s Blu-ray edition includes a handful of bonus features. Director Dallas Jenkins is joined by producer Kevin Downes for an audio commentary track. A quintet of short featurettes offers some standard behind-the-scenes footage. Bloopers and deleted scenes round out the package. The Best Christmas Pageant Ever , well-acted (especially by Beatrice Schneider as the Herdmans’ de facto “mother” figure, Imogene) deserves recognition as a new holiday classic. When you watch the trailer above, you might theorize immediately and say Meryl Streep has to be playing the gray-haired scientist, like I did, but that's not the case. Hoppers is about a group of scientists who invent a way to "hop" human minds into lifelike robotic animal bodies that can understand the animal world. Emily Charlton (Emily Blunt), Miranda's former junior assistant who is now a high-ranking executive for a luxury group with advertising dollars that Priestley sorely needs, soon confronts her. The Devil Wears Prada earned $326 million at the global box office and was a critical and commercial success. The Devil Wears Prada 2 is set to hit the theatres on May 1, 2026. Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery is slated to hit theaters on Nov. 26, before releasing on Netflix on Dec. 12, giving subscribers the opportunity to watch the third Benoit Blanc whodunnit, starring Daniel Craig as the renowned detective. It is not confirmed whether this will be his final case, or whether he will be back for another , but that hasn't stopped Johnson from plotting out the future – including who could join the cast. Each entry of the Knives Out franchise introduces a stacked ensemble alongside Craig's skillful sleuth. It is usually a mix of veteran actors and rising talent, with some of the most prominent cast members including, but not limited to, Chris Evans, Jamie Lee Curtis, Kate Hudson, Dave Bautista, Josh Brolin, Glenn Close, and Jeremy Renner in a new expanded role . Given the all-star talent Johnson has managed to secure up to now, people might be curious about which names could possibly be left on his dream casting list. They need wonder no more, because IndieWire put the question to the filmmaker directly, prompting him to reveal: "There are so many great actors I'd like to work with. But, yes, if you're reading this, Meryl Streep, I feel like you'd slot into a murder mystery very well." "If Lorne can do it, then, goddamn, so can we," he quipped, giving a shoutout to Lorne Michaels – the creator and long-time executive producer of the iconic sketch-comedy show Saturday Night Live ( SNL ). He was a central figure at the televised 50th Anniversary Special earlier this year, which brought back a variety of its top-rated talent alongside a few notable newcomers, including Streep, who made her first-ever appearance on the show. The award-winning actress starred in a new edition of a well-known recurring "Close Encounter" sketch with Kate McKinnon, Pedro Pascal, Woody Harrelson, Jon Hamm, and Aidy Bryant. Meryl Streep Is No Stranger to Sleuthing Meryl Streep as Loretta Durkin in Only Murders in the Building Patrick Harbron/Hulu Meryl Streep has had a decades-long, highly decorated career that has seen her star in everything from Kramer vs. Kramer and Sophie's Choice to The Devil Wears Prada and Mamma Mia! In recent years, she has become associated with sleuthing due to her recurring role as Loretta Durkin in the hit mystery-comedy series Only Murders in the Building . Her character regularly pops up alongside the main trio of Oliver Putnam, Charles-Haden Savage, and Mabel Mora, played by Martin Short, Steve Martin, and Selena Gomez, respectively, due to her close connection to the amateur true-crime podcasters. While she is much more adept at sleuthing, a role in Knives Out would likely put her in the frame as a suspect. Johnson previously admitted to having no idea what he would do for a fourth entry, but it seems that now Wake Up Dead Man is on the horizon, ideas have started to formulate and Streep is his primary target should another film get greenlit. The Rotten Tomatoes score for the latest installment teases another must-see Knives Out mystery , so now everything hinges on its performance in theaters and on streaming – the latter of which fulfills the two-sequel deal Johnson signed with Netflix back in 2021. By Shaun Kitchener Published: 12 November 2025 If the wait for The Devil Wears Prada 2 seems to be moving at a glacial pace, fear not: the newly released teaser trailer for the upcoming sequel is sure to help take the edge off. Meryl Streep and Anne Hathaway both feature in the brief clip released today, which teases the return of Miranda Priestly and Andy Sachs. We're still six months away from the sequel to The Devil Wears Prada landing in cinemas, but the new promo promises a fresh team-up in the hallowed halls of Runway magazine. In the teaser, a pair of extremely fabulous red shoes can be seen strutting through an open-plan office, before they step into an elevator and are revealed to belong to Streep's Miranda. She's dressed in sunglasses, a black-and-white skirt, a black top and a red belt (not blue, not turquoise, not lapis, not even cerulean). Before the elevator doors can close, she's joined by Hathaway's Andy, who says simply: "Miranda." What to Read Next "Took you long enough," Miranda quips, as Andy puts her own pair of sunglasses on. Madonna's 'Vogue' soundtracks the scene, which segues into a title card and the promised release date of May 1. Emily Blunt and Stanley Tucci are also part of the headline cast for the movie, reprising their iconic roles of Emily and Nigel. 20th Century Studios Related: The Devil Wears Prada 2 gets exciting update after 19-year wait for fans – but one star won't return Joining them are Kenneth Branagh, Tracie Thoms, Tibor Feldman, Lucy Liu and Bridgerton favourite Simone Ashley . Lady Gaga is also slated to appear, and the likes of Sydney Sweeney and even Donatella Versace have been spotted on set too. Speaking to ELLE about her return, Blunt said: “It’s terribly moving. Because [the original] changed everything. David Frankel [director] changed my life by casting me when I was an unknown. "I’d been working, but no one knew who I was, and he was so sure that he wanted me in the movie, from a taped reading. That meant a huge amount to me.” 20th Century Studios Related: Best film and TV tours for 2025 She added: "It did leave the door open for people to see me as more than a British period drama girl. It paved the way for character roles, which is all I wanted. I didn’t want to be an ingenue." The 2006 film, which was based on a 2003 novel by Lauren Weisberger, has also recently become a hit West End musical with original music by Elton John. Desperate Housewives and Ugly Betty icon Vanessa Williams currently plays Miranda, with Mamma Mia: I Have A Dream winner Stevie Doc taking over as Andy. The Devil Wears Prada 2 is out on May 1. LogOut HOMEPAGE Celebrity Kate Winslet Recalls Shielding Her Nipples From King Charles WHOOPS! The actress didn’t know she would be meeting the royal when she chose her outfit. Eboni Boykin-Patterson Entertainment Reporter Published Nov. 19 2025 11:53AM EST Comments Britain’s own Kate Winslet very nearly made a shocking first impression on King Charles. Winslet, 50, told Jimmy Kimmel the story of her first meeting then-Prince Charles in 1995. “It was a royal premiere of Sense and Sensibility when I was only 20. And I sort of hadn’t realized that we were really going to meet him. And so I forgot about the fact that I really was wearing a kind of a transparent lace outfit,” she began the story. Winslet didn’t know she would meet then-Prince Charles before she chose her outfit for the 1995 premiere of "Sense and Sensibility." Tom Wargacki/WireImage “Thank god I’d worn a coat because as he’s making his way towards me, I’m like, ‘nipples, nipples, nipples,’” she continued. While Winslet’s see-through lace ensemble was thicker to cover her bottom half, it achieved significantly less up top. Winslet told Kimmel she was handed her cover-up just in time. “Someone just went ‘Coat!’ And I went, ‘Your majesty.’ I’m like basically covering myself in a cape.” Kimmel quipped, “That makes me feel sorry for the king because he’s the only one that doesn’t get to see nipples. Watching everybody curtsy all the time—there’s no fun in that.” The Regime star said she had a less eventful meetup with King Charles this past June. Meryl Streep, David Beckham, and more also attended the star-studded event to mark the 35th anniversary of the King’s Foundation. It wasn’t totally without hiccups, however, Winslet shared. Winslet made sure to wear an outfit she wouldn't have to cover her nipples in when she met the King again in June. WPA Pool/Getty Images “When Meryl and I were walking, she says to me, ‘Do you think we have to curtsy?’ And I said, ‘We absolutely have to curtsy.’ She was like, ‘OK, is it a big curtsy? Is it—like, what do we do?’ I said, ‘I don’t know’...She was like, ‘I don’t know if we need to do that.’ There was a big panic.” Winslet said she and Meryl Streep had a “big panic” over whether or not to curtsy when they met the royal this summer. WPA Pool/Getty Images The stars managed to pull off the interaction without offending or flashing anyone. Even if it had gone wrong, Winslet said she likes to go first in her party when it comes to doing scary things in public. “I’m always trying to volunteer to go first because I feel like leadership is important, and someone has to get it wrong,” she said. “And it is usually me that does, so I don’t mind taking the hit.” Eboni Boykin-Patterson Entertainment Reporter EB_hyphenate eboni.boykin-patterson@thedailybeast.com Got a tip? By Stefania Sarrubba Published: 20 November 2025 Amanda Seyfried wants a third Mamma Mia! to happen just like the rest of us as she's put together her dream cast for the possible threequel. The Mean Girls star, next to be seen in Mona Fastvold's musical drama The Testament of Ann Lee , has confirmed that Mamma Mia 3 is not off the table. "Of course it's not off the table, it's searing a hole into the table," she said of a continuation of the Greece-set story for her character Sophie (via Entertainment Tonight ). What to Read Next "Maybe I should just be coy, or maybe I'm just naïve, but I'm pretty sure Mamma Mia 3 is a done deal," she continued Weighing in about where a third story could lead Sophie, Seyfried said she "would love" to see more of her protagonist with her children. Universal Pictures Related: Christine Baranski clears up Mamma Mia 3 update – and fans will be disappointed "I love portraying a mum, so I would love to see Sophie with her kids," she said. Released in 2008, Mamma Mia! centred on Sophie's wedding and search for her biological dad. Seyfried starred opposite Meryl Streep in the role of her mum Donna, the manager of a hotel on a fictional Greek island. Ten years after the OG, sequel Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again saw much of the cast returning for one more adventure, with singer Cher joining the cast. And it looks like Seyfried has just another singer in mind for the threequel as she explained she's "all for" more female artists to get on board. As to who she would like to see next to Sophie in Mamma Mia 3 , Seyfried called on a pop star and a fellow actor to join the cast of the musical. "Maybe [Sophie] has a cousin she hasn't seen in a while, that could be Sabrina Carpenter," she said. "And then Sydney Sweeney could show up... There's a bunch of girls that really want to be a part of it, and I'm all for it." Universal Pictures Despite Seyfried's enthusiasm, there hasn't been an official confirmation that the third film is a go so far. Earlier this year, co-star Christine Baranski, who plays Tanya in both films, clarified rumours of a third film happening after she said she met up with producer Judy Craymer. "No [developments], but the last time I said anything, it went viral, and it was only a speculation," she told RadioTimes in May. "But I'm friends with Judy Craymer, who's the producer and initiator of Mamma Mia! , and she very much wants to do number three." Published Wed, 12 Nov 2025 18:02:03 -0600 by Kaitlyn Booth | Comments Article Summary The Devil Wears Prada 2 teaser trailer, poster, logo, and image have been officially released by 20th Century. The long-awaited sequel arrives in theaters on May 1, 2026, nearly twenty years after the original film's debut. Meryl Streep, Anne Hathaway, Emily Blunt, and Stanley Tucci reprise their iconic roles in this highly anticipated sequel. The sequel promises to explore today's evolving fashion landscape and the changing world of print journalism. Another project that has been hanging out in development hell for over a decade is finally making its way onto to the big screen. When The Devil Wears Prada was released in 2006, no one was expecting it to have the cultural impact that it did. It wasn't even a critical smash hit at the time, though it was a commercial success, making over $325 million at the box office on a budget of ~$41 million. Not only was it a commercial success, but the film has also influenced countless memes and jokes to the point that some people might not even know that the Chanel boots joke is coming from this film. A sequel was first teased in 2013, but failed to get off the ground. The cast has been asked about a sequel on and off ever since, but it wasn't until July 2024 that the sequel was confirmed, and they were bringing back much of the main cast from the previous film. The Devil Wears Prada 2 will be released on May 1, 2026, so the film will be released the weekend before the Met Gala. The first teaser trailer, poster, logo, and image were all released today. The way we view fashion and body image has changed significantly since the early 2000s, not to mention the state of print journalism, providing ample material for this movie to explore. A teaser for the sequel, set for May 1, 2026, showcases Meryl Streep's Miranda Priestly and Anne Hathaway's Andy Sachs reuniting. The clip hints at a new era for the fashion industry, with fans eagerly anticipating the return of the original cast and new additions like Lady Gaga. After years of speculation, whispers from set photos, and a handful of cryptic Anne Hathaway posts, The Devil Wears Prada 2 is officially here, or at least, its first teaser is. The sequel’s title may be straightforward, but many fans are already wishing it had borrowed from Lauren Weisberger’s follow-up novel, Revenge Wears Prada: The Devil Returns. Because, really, who’s the revenge, and who’s the devil this time? The teaser doesn’t answer that, but it offers a stylish hint. Set to Madonna’s “Vogue,” the clip focuses almost entirely on the clicking of Miranda Priestly’s heels echoing through what appears to be Runway’s glassy new headquarters. Then comes the elevator moment that sent social media spiraling: Andy Sachs, now looking every inch the power player she once feared, steps in beside her old boss. “Miranda,” she says coolly. Behind oversized sunglasses, Meryl Streep ’s Miranda simply replies, “Took you long enough.” It’s a line loaded with history, and irony. If the first film was about Andy trying to survive Miranda’s world, this one might just flip the dynamic entirely. Is Andy now the devil in Prada, or is Miranda still running the show from the top floor? The teaser wisely keeps those answers tucked under a designer coat. Set for a May 1, 2026 release, the sequel reunites Streep, Hathaway, Emily Blunt, and Stanley Tucci, with David Frankel once again directing from a script by Aline Brosh McKenna. The new cast includes Kenneth Branagh, Simone Ashley, Lucy Liu, Justin Theroux, and Lady Gaga , who’s already been photographed in full glam on set. By Joe Anderton Published: 08 November 2025 Stephen Graham has had a busy 2025, appearing in A Thousand Blows , Springsteen: Deliver Me From Nowhere , and a little-known show called Adolescence . But he isn't slowing down – far from it in fact. The prolific actor has been confirmed as one of the cast members for Ibelin , the real-life story of a Norwegian man named Mats Steen. Steen suffered from degenerative muscle disease which severely limited his ability to participate in every day activities. Instead, he decided to pour most of his time and effort into his World of Warcraft character, the titular Ibelin. What to Read Next He also kept a blog where he documented his life living with the condition, known as Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Following his passing, he became a legend in the game's community, and was honoured with a gravestone within the virtual realm by creators Blizzard. Marc Piasecki // Getty Images Related: UK film release dates As reported by Variety , Graham has been confirmed for the "inspirational" film, alongside Sir Anthony Hopkins, Charlie Plummer, Toni Collette, Isabela Merced, and Maisy Stella. The Imitation Game 's Morten Tyldum is directing the movie, which is based on a script from Ilaria Bernardini and Hossein Amini. The film is set to explore both Steen's family, as well as the World of Warcraft players who became fans of Steen and his digital alter-ego. Steen's story was previously immortalised in the Netflix documentary The Remarkable Life of Ibelin , which was released in October 2024. The film used real-life text logs from Ibelin's guild, as well as character models and other assets from World of Warcraft , to tell its story It was highly acclaimed, sitting at a near-perfect 97% positive score on Rotten Tomatoes from 60 critic reviews. Kevin Mazur // Getty Images Related: Quentin Tarantino's two-part "masterpiece" Kill Bill is getting epic new release with unseen footage Meanwhile, Graham is set to continue to explore the themes included in Adolescence through the book Letters to Our Sons . "After the huge impact of Adolescence , I realised there was a greater need for communication between fathers and sons," the actor said. "There is arguably an even bigger disconnect than ever before. "I would love to help create more opportunity for fathers to reach out to their sons and carry on the conversation." The new edition of Living Legends is here! Advertise on Cineuropa Logos and Banners Links previous next PRODUCTION / FUNDING France / Norway Vendôme Pictures and Pathé reunite for Morten Tyldum’s Ibelin by Davide Abbatescianni 07/11/2025 - The star-studded cast is led by Charlie Plummer, Stephen Graham, Toni Collette, Isabela Merced, Maisy Stella and Anthony Hopkins l-r: Actors Charlie Plummer (© John Sears), Stephen Graham (© Bryan Berlin) and Toni Collette (© Gage Skidmore) Academy Award-winning firms Vendôme Pictures and Pathé are set to collaborate once again following their partnership on CODA , which won three Oscars. The two banners have announced Ibelin , directed by Oscar nominee Morten Tyldum ( The Imitation Game [ + see also: film review trailer making of film profile ] , Passengers , Silo ). The film will star Charlie Plummer ( The Long Walk , Lean on Pete [ + see also: film review trailer film profile ] ), Stephen Graham ( Adolescence [ + see also: trailer series profile ] , Boiling Point [ + see also: series review series profile ] , The Irishman , Rocketman [ + see also: film review trailer interview: Dexter Fletcher film profile ] ), Toni Collette ( Wayward , Hereditary , Knives Out ), Isabela Merced ( The Last of Us , Superman ), Maisy Stella ( My Old Ass ) and Anthony Hopkins ( The Father [ + see also: film review trailer interview: Florian Zeller film profile ] , The Two Popes [ + see also: film review trailer interview: Fernando Meirelles film profile ] ). (The article continues below - Commercial information) Black Bear is handling international sales and will introduce the title to buyers at the American Film Market (11-16 November), with CAA Media Finance repping US rights. Principal photography is expected to take place in Europe in spring/summer 2026. Penned by BAFTA nominee Ilaria Bernardini ( Citadel: Diana [ + see also: series review series profile ] ) and Academy Award nominee Hossein Amini ( The Snowman [ + see also: trailer film profile ] , Drive , The Wings of the Dove ), the screenplay is based on the blog “Musings of Life” by Mats Steen , whose story forms the core of the film. Steen lived with a degenerative muscular disease and spent much of his social life engaged in the online realm of the game World of Warcraft , where he was known as “Ibelin”, a figure admired for his humour, empathy and leadership. The project examines how his online persona revealed – and expanded – the emotional reality of his offline life. The official synopsis describes the pic as “a celebration of life – tender, funny and profoundly moving; a heartfelt family story intertwined with an epic adventure that explores the power of friendship and the invisible threads that connect us all”. Notably, a documentary on the same subject helmed by Benjamin Ree , The Remarkable Life of Ibelin [ + see also: film review trailer interview: Benjamin Ree film profile ] , premiered last year at Sundance, where it scooped two prizes in the World Cinema Documentary Competition: the Audience Award and the Directing Award. It later went on to receive a Peabody Award at the 85th annual ceremony. The feature helped bring wider international recognition to Mats Steen’s story and the emotional resonance of his online community. Ibelin is being produced by Philippe Rousselet and Fabrice Gianfermi for Vendôme Pictures (France), Jérôme Seydoux for Pathé (France), and Morten Tyldum and Guri Neby for Neby-Tyldum AS. Vendôme and Pathé are financing the feature. Sarah Finn ( Everything Everywhere All at Once , Crash ) serves as casting director and executive producer. Speaking about the project, Rousselet said: “ Ibelin is a sensational story that will be told by a remarkable group of storytellers – first and foremost, Morten, who has a rare ability to evoke emotions with films like The Imitation Game and epics such as Passengers and Silo . We have assembled a formidable cast and, with our frequent collaborators at Pathé and the team at Black Bear, are confident that this will be a film that will resonate with buyers and audiences everywhere.” (The article continues below - Commercial information) Did you enjoy reading this article? But looking back, one show airing that fall feels like the kind of serialized thriller that would be dominating today’s streaming charts or thriving on a premium cable network . Instead, it lasted just a single season. Hostages is a tense, ambitious drama that was abruptly cancelled before it could fully tap into its potential. The series marked Toni Collette ’s return to television after her acclaimed run on United States of Tara , and it featured one of her most underrated performances . At a time when network TV still relied heavily on case-of-the-week storytelling , Hostages dared to embrace a tightly serialized, high-stakes political thriller format which fits far more naturally in today’s landscape. In many ways, the show was simply ahead of its time , and it's first and only season is free to watch on Tubi . What Is Toni Collette's Forgotten Thriller 'Hostages' About? The premise alone set Hostages apart from almost everything else on network TV . Collette stars as Dr. Ellen Sanders, a world-renowned surgeon chosen to operate on the President of the United States. However, the night before the operation, her family is taken hostage by a group of masked intruders led by rogue FBI agent Duncan Carlisle ( Dylan McDermott , years before he would headline FBI: Most Wanted ). Their simple yet horrifying demand is that Ellen must sabotage the operation and let the president die — or her family will pay the price. On its own, it’s an instantly gripping setup and almost feels more like a movie premise , and certainly not something for network TV in 2013. But stretched over 15 episodes, each one representing a single day in the story’s timeline, it becomes clear that Hostages has all the makings of the gritty, serialized limited series we see today. As strong as the initial hook is, it’s only the beginning . While Ellen scrambles to protect her family and stall for time, the conspiracy behind the assassination plot expands into something far larger and far more personal than she or the audience ever expects, especially when it comes to Duncan. The show’s tension hinges on the shifting leverage between Ellen and Duncan , slowly revealing his motives and blurring the line between hero and villain in ways that keep the stakes escalating until the very end. Posts By Jake Hodges Jul 25, 2025 What also sets Hostages apart is how many storylines it juggles without losing momentum. There are a lot of secrets being kept in Hostages , which helps keep the tension alive from all angles. Tate Donovan ’s Brian Sanders carries secrets that threaten to unravel the family from the inside, while Billy Brown , Sandrine Holt , and Jeremy Bobb bring texture to the people orbiting Duncan’s plan. As their motivations and betrayals come into focus, the series expands beyond a simple hostage thriller into a broader web of political corruption , personal sacrifice and impossible choices. Instead of relying on procedural beats, Hostages takes its time peeling back the layers of its characters, making each one as complex and conflicted as possible. The series weaves those personal complications into a slow-burn narrative that feels far more ambitious and far more serialized than anything else on CBS at the time. Toni Collette and Dylan McDermott’s Tense Dynamic Makes 'Hostages' Worth Watching Dylan McDermott as Duncan and Toni Collette as Ellen in Hostages Image via CBS What truly elevates Hostages beyond its intriguing premise is the electric push-and-pull between Toni Collette and Dylan McDermott . As Ellen Sanders and Duncan Carlisle, they’re two brilliant people forced into opposite corners of an impossible situation. Their on-screen chemistry crackles as they constantly battle for the upper hand, both desperate to save their families even as they find themselves strangely understanding each other. The result is a series of leverage shifts, as one moment Duncan holds all the cards and the next, Ellen turns the tables. Collette’s movie-star presence grounds it all, and she plays Ellen as a woman who becomes someone different with her family, at work, and with her captors, slowly discovering her strength in the most destabilizing circumstances imaginable. Both actors have spoken openly about what drew them to the show, and it’s clear why. At the time, the series felt far fresher and more layered than most network dramas . In an interview with Channel 4 , McDermott said he was “instantly intrigued” by Duncan’s morally gray nature and how he walked the line between good and bad. Collette praised how “the characters are so complex and three-dimensional and relatable and real.” That kind of language is commonplace in today’s prestige television , but for CBS in 2013, it signaled that Hostages belonged to a different era of storytelling, and perhaps, one that hadn’t fully arrived yet. Despite all of this, the show still ended after one season. Ratings dropped sharply after the premiere , which is especially unfortunate because the series felt like it had great potential for several more seasons. In the binge-watching era, Hostages likely would have thrived alongside politically-charged hits like The Night Agent or The Diplomat , which blend political intrigue, family drama and character-driven tension. The show’s layered mystery and moral complexity feel far more aligned with today’s streaming landscape. In hindsight, it’s clear Hostages was built for more than a single season. The writing is smart and deeply character-driven in ways network audiences may not have been fully primed for yet. Released today, its intricate plot and stacked cast would fit seamlessly on a major streamer and would almost certainly find the wider audience it always deserved. Thankfully, with streaming platforms giving overlooked series a second life , you can watch the entire season on Tubi and see for yourself just how ahead of its time Hostages really was. Oscar nominee Toni Collette ( Knives Out ) and Supergirl star Milly Alcock are teaming up to star in survival thriller Hot Mother , which is being lined up for a 2026 shoot in Australia. In Hot Mother , a mother and daughter visit a remote wellness spa for the weekend in an attempt to reconnect. But their time together quickly turns into a physical and psychological fight for survival when they get trapped in a sauna where no one can hear their cries for help. Lucy Knox’s feature debut will follow her short of the same name which she wrote and directed and which premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival in 2020. Bankside Films is handling worldwide sales and co-repping North America with CAA Media Finance ahead of next week’s American Film Market. The Australian movie will be produced by Sarah Shaw and Anna McLeish for Carver Films and Oscar-winner Alex Coco for Rapt Films. Coco most recently produced Sean Baker’s Anora , having previously collaborated with the director on Red Rocket and The Florida Project . Carver produced Run Rabbit Run which released on Netflix worldwide after its Sundance premiere in 2023 and is also known for producing movies including Sundance horror Relic and acclaimed Cannes drama Snowtown . Collette and Jen Turner will serve as executive producers under Collette’s Vocab Films banner. Ruby Monette-Meadow will also executive-produce. The film will have major production investment from Screen Australia, in association with Screen NSW. Financed in association with VicScreen, local distribution will come from Maslow Entertainment. Muriel’s Wedding and Knives Out star Collette is known for genre hits including The Sixth Sense and Hereditary . House Of The Dragon star Alcock, who recently starred in Netflix series Sirens , is currently taking on the title role in DC Entertainment’s Supergirl , which is released next year. Anna McLeish and Sarah Shaw of Carver Films said: “As producers with a strong track record of launching Australian filmmakers, we’ve been aware of Lucy’s exceptional talent as a writer-director for many years. She’s beyond ready to bring Hot Mother to life for audiences worldwide, with its thrilling screenplay and incredible cast.” Alex Coco commented: “Lucy is a filmmaker’s filmmaker, exactly the directors that I’m most committed to working with. With our two lead actresses, this film will play wide globally, and introduce a new and fresh voice to the directing game.” Stephen Kelliher of Bankside Films added: “We were sold on Hot Mother from the title alone but discovering Lucy Knox’s incredible short and reading the screenplay solidified our immense passion for this story. With character and mother-daughter relationships at its heart, the film will thrill audiences with its edge-of-your-seat take on a survival story.” Toni Collette is represented by CAA, Finley Management and United Management. Milly Alcock is represented by Entertainment360, CAA, Curtis Brown and Goodman, Genow. Lucy Knox is represented by Dissident and Gochman Law Group. Alex Coco is represented by Dissident, CAA and Lichter, Grossman. In the case of Alex Pettyfer ’s ( Magic Mike ) character in the upcoming film, Under the Stars , it crashes into his life in a most unexpected way. Set for an on-demand arrival courtesy of AURA Entertainment on November 11, your new rom-com obsession is the focus of our latest showcase in our ongoing Collider Exclusive Preview event. Featuring an absolutely dynamite cast that includes Toni Collette ( Hereditary ), Andy Garcia ( The Godfather Part III ), Eva De Dominici ( The Fragility of Bodies ), and Vincent Riotta ( Under the Tuscan Sun ), the Michelle Danner -helmed feature has everything you’d want in a romantic comedy and then some. In a flirty and fun moment between the blossoming couple at the center of the film, De Dominici and Pettyfer’s characters sit down for dinner in our exclusive first look at Under the Stars . Sipping their wine, the pair muse over the idea of “the one,” with each of them dishing out their hottest takes and strongest beliefs about what makes long-term couples go the distance. As the film’s primary couple digs into one another’s love lives, the story’s secondary couple, played by Collette and Garcia, share a nice bottle of red and discuss their previous romantic shortcomings and mistakes. Additionally, our exclusive first-look image of Under the Stars sees the romance between Collette and Garcia’s characters continue to blossom. Dressed in a navy blue suit, Garcia’s character can be seen sitting next to and directly addressing Collette’s who, in a white ensemble, flashes an ear-to-ear grin as she looks at someone off camera. What Is ‘Under the Stars’ About? andy-garcia-toni-collette-under-the-stars Following the successful release of his first novel, an author (Pettyfer) hits a wall of writer's block and can’t seem to get his follow-up book up and running. Just as his professional life begins to go down the tubes, his long-term relationship also hits a rough patch, leading him to travel across the ocean to Italy for a little break and maybe some inspiration. While there, his path crosses with a young woman (De Dominici), who challenges everything he thought he knew about love and life. If you’re looking for a dreamy rom-com that will whisk you away to a gorgeous setting, look no further than this one. Speaking about where we'll find his character at the beginning of the film and why Italy ends up meaning so much to him, Pettyfer told us, “I think Italy represents a kind of beautiful contradiction for him — it’s both an escape and a confrontation . He goes there chasing quiet, but what he really finds is movement — colour, spontaneity, a culture that refuses to let him stay numb . His life back home has become all head, no heart; Italy flips that balance. So when he meets Arianna, he’s already standing on emotional quicksand — a little lost, a little open. She doesn’t just knock him off his feet; she reminds him what it feels like to have them on the ground again .” Check out our sneak peek and first look image of Under the Stars above, and see it on demand on November 11. Next Friday, inside the world-acclaimed National Institute of Dramatic Art’s Parade Theatre in Sydney’s Kensington, the 22-strong Class of 2025 – whittled down from 1000 applicants – will stage their “showcase”. After three gruelling years, the mostly 20-somethings will sing, dance and act in a series of vignettes before an invitation-only audience of potential agents, talent scouts and industry heavyweights. They’re a diverse cohort. Quinn Chambers from suburban Brisbane gave up a carpentry apprenticeship to be there. Nyasha Ogden, a Larrakia woman and yoga enthusiast from Darwin, wants to represent First Nations people through her art. Charlie Chandler, a fifth-generation outback stockman, quit the dust to act. NIDA 2023 graduate Jack Patten is starring in a TV remake of Robin Hood. Credit: Aleksandar Letic/MGM+ “We’re not looking for great actors,” says NIDA’s head of acting, John Bashford. “We’re looking for people with an innate sense of storytelling who can elicit an emotional response [from their audience]. Along with technique, we teach them stamina, resourcefulness, resilience and how to create opportunities in an industry that’s notoriously tough.” In June, The Hollywood Reporter ranked NIDA the world’s 14th-best drama school – the only Australian entry in a list of 25. Its famous former alumni include Cate Blanchett, Mel Gibson, Judy Davis, Geoffrey Rush, Sarah Snook, Baz Luhrmann, Toni Collette, Hugo Weaving and Richard Roxburgh. Within a year of graduating in 2023, Jack Patten had landed the titular role in the new blockbuster TV series Robin Hood . Meanwhile, Class of 2018’s Yerin Ha will be taking on the female lead, Sophie Baek (Benedict’s love interest), in the next series of Bridgerton , airing on Netflix in January. Loading In the 2008 documentary Acting Class of 1977 , Mel Gibson – now reportedly worth an estimated $650 million – revealed to writer, director and fellow graduate Sally McKenzie that he’d hated the tap-dancing classes and was almost “kicked out” but felt, ultimately, that he’d been “exposed to things that I never, ever would have ... otherwise”. “We were taught to make up stories, get with friends ... create something,” Baz Luhrmann told American 60 Minutes in 2024. “I had an idea that I would take the Greek myth and … set it in the world of ballroom dancing. That little play went for about 30 minutes. One of his most underrated series, "The United States of Tara," aired on Showtime for three seasons, from 2009-2011. On the surface, "The United States of Tara" is your average family comedy-drama about the Gregsons, who hail from a Kansas town. Toni Collette plays Tara, and John Corbett, AKA Aidan from "Sex and the City" and "And Just Like That," is her husband, Max. They have two teenage kids, Kate and Marshall, played by Brie Larson (the future Ms. Marvel and Academy Award winner for "Room") and Keir Gilchrist (who would go on to star on the Netflix series "Atypical," which ran from 2017 to 2021 ). Rosemarie DeWitt, who appears in "Mad Men" and "Little Fires Everywhere," plays Tara's sister Charmaine. Beneath their regular suburban problems, they have to deal with something much more complicated — Tara has Dissociative Identity Disorder. The United States of Tara is a showcase for Toni Collette's amazing range Showtime In his role as producer, Steven Spielberg spearheaded "The United States of Tara," reaching out to "Juno" scribe Diablo Cody to write a show about Dissociative Identity Disorder (per The Wall Street Journal ). "The United States of Tara" was a showcase for the brilliant Toni Collette. Tara has multiple personalities that she refers to as "alters," of all ages and lifestyles. One minute she can be a sweet-as-pie 1950s housewife, the next a rebellious teenager or a crass Vietnam veteran. As the seasons progress, more alters are revealed. Her alters always show up at the wrong time, and it's usually the one least ideal for the situation. Although "The United States of Tara" only lasted three seasons, it could have easily run longer as Tara's alters evolved or came more under control. The chaotic situations that the alters caused, and the friction they created within her family, were always wickedly funny and equally moving, and could have continued to be so. Collette received both an Emmy and a Golden Globe award for playing the series' title role. She has continued to take on meaty television roles, including standout turns on "Unbelievable," as a detective investigating sex crimes, and the recent "Wayward," as a cult leader. It all makes a great foundation for an eerie psychological thriller and Wayward is just that. The Netflix show focusses on a school for troubled teens whose charismatic founder is more of a cult leader than a principal. Just eight episodes long with lots of heart-pounding chases, I devoured the series in a week. It starts with a broken window and a petrified teenage boy escaping the school. Soon after an officer moves into the town with his wife and the mystery begins as he discovers the school and its founder are darker and more twisted than they at first seem. Comedian Mae Martin is the creator and protagonist of the show and they are partly what is so captivating about the series. Apart from the incredible performance by Toni Collette, who plays Evelyn, the school’s leader, Mae’s character is striking. The non-binary actor plays a non-binary cop, married to his pregnant wife. This portrayal of queer characters is refreshing to watch and even more so because their queerness is not the star of the show but simply a detail of the character. As the new cop in town, they are the only person in law enforcement trying to dig up what is going on in the school. When two best friends get locked up there and try to fight the brainwashing tactics, they team up with the cop to uncover the Tall Pines Academy’s twisted ways. But for Alex, the cop, the story hits a little closer to home as his wife’s secrets begin to unfold. There is no doubt the show is unsettling and no matter how unlikeable Toni Collette’s character is, she is captivating. And it is upsetting to think that leaders like her and schools like that shown in Wayward exist. In fact, Mae Martin revealed that the story is inspired by their own real-life experiences and the reports of a school system eerily similar to Tall Pines. Creepy and unbelievable but it kept me watching day after day. They’ll play a mother and daughter who visit a remote wellness spa for the weekend in an attempt to reconnect. But their time together quickly turns into a physical and psychological fight for survival when they get trapped in a sauna where no one can hear their cries for help. Production is slated to begin next year in Australia, with writer-director Lucy Knox making her feature debut, based on her 2020 short film of the same name. Night Shyamalan's "The Sixth Sense" needs no introduction. The psychological horror, which was released during the summer of 1999, became something of a sleeper hit while cementing Shyamalan's strengths as a director with an intuitive bent for surprise twists. "The Sixth Sense" uses gradually escalating dread to build its central tragedy, and knowing its big twist in advance doesn't detract from the experience. If anything, it adds thematic layers to the plight of the troubled Cole (Haley Joel Osment), while highlighting the unique anxieties of life during the cusp of the millennium. Toni Collette's nuanced performance as Cole's mother, Lynn Sear, earned her a Best Supporting Actress nomination at the Academy Awards, where horror awards are rarely recognized. Yet Collette wasn't actually aware that "The Sixth Sense" was a horror movie during the time of filming. In an interview for the radio show Q with Tom Power , she explained that her initial understanding was that Shyamalan's film was a "spiritual" drama, and that the horror aspect of the narrative only dawned on her when she saw it being pieced together: "I haven't done that many [horror movies]. It's only a handful, and I don't like to watch them. But being in them is very different [...] I just thought ['The Sixth Sense'] was a beautiful spiritual story. I remember walking past a makeshift edit suite on set [...] And they were cutting the scene together where Hayley is at that girl's house, played by Mischa Barton [who plays the ghost of Kyra Collins]. And he walks past the bed, and she reaches out and grabs him. And the way it was shot, I was like, 'Oh, holy sh**. I think this is a horror movie!' [Laughs]." The Sixth Sense is much more than a ghost story Buena Vista Pictures Distribution While Collette's anecdote is chuckle-worthy, it is not far-fetched to frame "The Sixth Sense" as a spiritual story about death, suffering, and our inherent inability to communicate. "If we can't talk to each other, we're not gonna make it," Lynn gently tells Cole, as she can sense the growing divide that is preventing her from understanding his predicament. There is no grudge or ill will here, of course, but a general inability to lay one's soul bare. Cole's pain stems from his power to communicate with spirits, but this gift doesn't always translate to the living. While Malcom attempts to help the child overcome this hurdle, the full scope of the truth proves to be too harrowing by the end. In the abovementioned interview, Collette talks about the beauty inherent in such a layered exploration of emotions, which is also the case with Ari Aster's "Hereditary," a story as heartbreaking as it is terrifying : "The horror films that I've done are actually just like beautiful dramas that have an element that pushes people just a little bit further. Like 'Hereditary' is just a heartbreaking story about family grief and disconnection." While "Hereditary" explores the darkest aspects of familial bonds through a quasi-fantastical lens, "The Sixth Sense" uses Cole's communication with spirits to convey the wondrous and terrifying extremes of childhood. In Cole's case, seeing things nobody else can is a burden, and he often witnesses horrific aspects of life that no child should be exposed to . Can such a curse be channeled into a gift if Cole bravely helps those nobody else can? The answer is a hope-tinged yes, which is the quiet promise of Shyamalan's "The Sixth Sense." Recommended

Jordan Honored at 39th Annual American Cinematheque Awards November 21, 2025 Shawn Grant Michael B. Jordan was celebrated as a cinematic force at the 39th Annual American Cinematheque Awards on Thursday, November 20, 2025, at The Beverly Hilton. The actor received the prestigious American Cinematheque Award, while the Motion Picture Association was honored with the Power of Cinema Award, presented by Hill Valley. The event highlighted Jordan’s career achievements and his dedication to authentic storytelling. Tributes from Hollywood peers poured in. Ben Affleck called him “a young man with enormous talent and even more impressive character… I got to watch him navigate this world with grace and calm, and it has been one of the great joys of my career.” Mahershala Ali reflected, “Even as a young actor, he was able to channel something greater… Michael’s talent has always reflected the truth.” Octavia Spencer praised him as “a brilliant character actor with an unstoppable work ethic… you make a movie that withstands the test of time.” Tessa Thompson emphasized Jordan’s cultural impact: “Michael’s contribution to film expands visions, not just of Black masculinity, but of the Black family… You embody excellence without ego.” Bradley Cooper added, “You’ve become a hero to so many, not just because of the characters you play, but because of who you are… You are shaping the culture, lifting spirits, and redefining what it means to be a hero.” Ryan Coogler underscored Jordan’s devotion to craft, citing his 12–15 hour training days, military training for roles, and ability to embody multiple characters in a single day. Jordan thanked Coogler and shared his vision for the future: “There’s so much going on in the world… I want to continue to be the light and hopefully spark that same light in you.” The evening featured a performance from Sinners , and was attended by luminaries including Angela Bassett, Tom Cruise, Daniel Kaluuya, Delroy Lindo, Phylicia Rashad, and Octavia Spencer. The ceremony honored Jordan’s remarkable career, his influence on Hollywood, and his commitment to inspiring the next generation of storytellers. Soul Food, 1997 This beloved family drama remains a staple during the holiday season. Starring Vanessa Williams, Vivica A Fox, Nia Long, Mekhi Phifer, and Michael Beach, the story follows a Chicago family trying to keep their traditions alive after the loss of their matriarch. The film blends love, conflict, healing, and the power of food as a bond that anchors everyone. It remains one of the most celebrated explorations of Black family life on screen. Johnson Family Vacation, 2004 Cedric the Entertainer leads this road trip comedy as a father determined to bring his family closer through a chaotic cross country drive to a reunion. The cast includes Vanessa Williams, Bow Wow, Solange, and Shannon Elizabeth. The laughs come fast as the Johnsons run into mishaps, eccentric characters, and plenty of tests of patience along the way. It is an easy crowd pleaser for the holiday weekend. Big Mommas House, 2000 Martin Lawrence steps into one of his most iconic roles in this family friendly hit. He plays an FBI agent who goes undercover as the beloved grandmother figure Big Momma in order to catch a criminal. The film features Nia Long, Paul Giamatti, Terrence Howard, and Jascha Washington. The humor, heart, and physical comedy make this an entertaining pick for a family movie night. Hidden Figures, 2016 Taraji P Henson, Octavia Spencer, and Janelle Monae star in the remarkable true story of three Black women whose brilliance helped drive the early success of the space program at NASA. The film brings both joy and heartfelt moments that connect with longtime fans. Black Nativity, 2013 Inspired by Langston Hughes work, this musical drama follows a teenage boy who travels to New York to spend Christmas with his estranged grandparents. Starring Forest Whitaker, Angela Bassett, Jennifer Hudson, Tyrese Gibson, Jacob Latimore, and Mary J Blige, the film blends gospel, family tension, faith, and redemption. It is a soulful holiday selection with powerful vocals and emotional resonance. Jordan received the American Cinematheque Award on Thursday in Beverly Hills, marking a milestone moment in his 20-year career and the acclaim surrounding Sinners. The night drew a heavy list of supporters — Ben Affleck, Mahershala Ali, Bradley Cooper, Daniel Kaluuya, Octavia Spencer, Tessa Thompson, Delroy Lindo, Phylicia Rashad and Irwin Winkler — with video tributes from Angela Bassett and Tom Cruise. Cruise praised Jordan’s evolution, saying, “I admire your talent, your dedication, your constant willingness to learn and push the boundaries of storytelling.” The program opened with Miles Caton, Ludwig Göransson and Raphael Saadiq performing Sinners’ standout track I Lied to You . Affleck recounted seeking Jordan out after Fruitvale Station, admitting Jordan soon needed little guidance and adding, “I got to watch him navigate this world with grace and calm.” Thompson joked that her on-screen romance with Jordan across the Creed films is “the longest relationship that either of us has ever been in,” while Cooper described himself as simply “a dedicated fan.” Kaluuya reflected on Black Panther and Jordan’s discipline on set, calling him “a movie star… who keeps showing us he’s an artist as well.” Ryan Coogler presented the honour, recalling their first meeting and telling the room, “I think you’re a star. Let’s do this project together and show the world.” Jordan, visibly emotional, said, “Man, nobody warns you how crazy this is… now I want to go do something else, like what’s next?” Looking back, he credited The Wire for igniting his drive and Coogler for helping him find his voice: “Finding a collaborator like him early in my career changed everything for me.” The evening also included Donna Langley presenting the Power of Cinema Award to MPA chairman Charles H. Share on Facebook Post Google Preferred Share to Flipboard Show more sharing options Email Share on LinkedIn Pin it Submit to Reddit Post to Tumblr Share on WhatsApp Print This Page 'Last Flight Out'; Sam Hargrave Katie Graves EXCLUSIVE: Following the successful launch of the Apple TV series The Last Frontier, Apple and director Sam Hargrave have found their next project on which to team. The director is in talks to helm an adaptation of the Dark Horse Comic Last Flight Out . Apple Original Films landed the package, which sources say was in the seven-figure range, and will develop along with Chernin Entertainment. The film is being adapted from Marc Guggenheim ’s acclaimed graphic novel published by Dark Horse and illustrated by Eduardo Ferigato. Hargrave will produce along with Chernin Entertainment’s Peter Chernin and David Ready as well Dark Horse Entertainment’s Mike Richardson and Keith Goldberg are set to produce. Guggenheim will adapt the script. Related Stories News Apple TV+ Rebrands To Apple TV, Dropping Plus Sign News Book-To-Movie Adaptations Coming Out In 2025 The novel series is about a father and daughter trying to reconcile at the end of the world. Apple and Chernin view this as a major event film and, given Hargrave’s track record with action-heavy pics like his Extraction films at Netflix and most recently The Last Frontier series, of which he helmed several episodes, Last Flight Out feels like the perfect project to add to his slate. Watch on Deadline The project also reunites Apple with Hargrave after the two worked together on the upcoming tentpole Matchbox starring John Cena. Hargrave is repped by WME. As for Guggenheim, he is best known for being one the architects of the Arrow -verse and has been on a roll of late, selling three pilots in the past six months. He is currently the writer and EP of the upcoming Netflix movie An Innocent Girl to be directed by Jaime Collett-Serra ( Carry-On ), which is in pre-production. He is repped by CAA, Cliff Roberts at Syndicate Entertainment and attorneys Wendy Kirk and Raymond Tramble. As for Chernin, the company has been busy after recently inking a first-look feature deal with Apple TV . Last Flight Out joins previously announced Five Secrets , a spec Apple preemptively purchased before Chernin could take it to market. Chernin Entertainment has produced multiple projects for Apple TV including the epic Chief of War starring Jason Momoa, the Emmy-nominated See also starring Momoa, NAACP Award-winning Truth Be Told starring Octavia Spencer and Gabrielle Union, and Emmy-winning documentary series The War for Football . File Photo by John Angelillo/UPI | License Photo Nov. 17 (UPI) -- Tom Cruise , Debbie Allen and Wynn Thomas received honorary Oscars during the 16th Governors Awards dinner gala on Sunday. Recipients are chosen by the Academy's Board of Governors for "extraordinary distinction in lifetime achievement in cinema and exceptional contributions to the state of motion picture arts and sciences," according to an official description . Cruise acknowledged his love of the film industry as he accepted his award from filmmaker Alejandro Inarittu. "When I was this little kid in this darkened theater and I remember that beam of light. It just cut across the room and I remember looking up and it seemed to me that it just exploded on the screen, and suddenly the world was so much larger than the one that I knew," he said. "You know, entire cultures and lives and landscapes and all of it was just unfolding in front of me." "And it sparked something in me," he continued. "It sparked a hunger. A hunger for adventure, a hunger for knowledge, a hunger to understand humanity, to create characters, to tell a story, to see the world.... And I have been following it ever since." Cynthia Erivo presented Allen's honor, while Octavia Spencer introduced Thomas' accolade. Allen, like Cruise, recalled her love of cinema sparking as a young child. "I've had a relationship since yes I was four years old, wanting to yes replace Shirley Temple ," she said during her acceptance speech. "Wishing I could have a Harry Belafonte blow my toe nail polish dry like he did with Dorothy Dandridge . Movies was a way in for me... We used to watch all the movies and our imaginations could go and wonder and we could see ourselves." In addition, Lily Thomas presented singer and actress Dolly Parton with this year's Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award. Parton, who has been struggling with health issues , accepted her accolade via a pre-recorded video. The ABC sitcom's Halloween episode had the internet buzzing when Gregory ( Tyler James Williams ) showed up on a camping trip dressed as Ryan Coogler alongside Janine ( Quinta Brunson ) as an Imax screen — “We’re Sinners ,” Janine says to an unimpressed Ava ( Janelle James ), who’s dressed as “Darth Ma,” a mash-up of Darth Vader and Octavia Spencer ’s Ma. At a recent FYC press event for Abbott Elementary , Brunson took a moment to do some light Oscar campaigning for Sinners — and revealed that the director was more than delighted by the tribute. Related Stories Why ‘Fallout’ Season 2 is vault-ing out of the winter awards cycle Did the Critics Choice Awards’ Best Song shortlist give us our first draft of the Oscar race? “He was so flattered! It was so sweet,” Brunson said. “I ran into him this weekend at the LACMA gala where he was being honored. He’s somebody I admire so much. I don’t admire many people — I actually admire that man. He came up to me as he was getting ready to give his speech and said his aunty sent him the episode. That’s how he found out about it, which is so special to me because we constantly say this is a show for family viewing. The fact that his aunt sent it to him was so special. It’s really exciting for us to celebrate any filmmakers in that way, but especially Ryan Coogler and to help cement him in culture.” Williams added that the Halloween tributes are always meant with genuine affection. “Every year we approach Halloween knowing that there’s going to be a moment we’re trying to capture,” he said. “People respond well hopefully. It’s all done out of love and it sounds like that was received.” Brunson also praised the storytelling of Sinners , which Coogler wrote and directed, calling it one of the most inclusive ensembles on screen today. “ Sinners is one of the most diverse casts we’ve seen in a long time, but that story is just good,” she explained. “The better the stories are, the more naturally you get diversity. We’re always going to need our industry to appreciate the storytelling of people of color, but a good story is a good story. As long as you have good, solid storytelling at the forefront, you can get away with anything. It’s not just about getting faces of color on the screen, it’s about a good story behind it.” The Abbott Elementary – Sinners crossover wasn’t on our bingo cards — but we’re absolutely here for it. By Brandon Caldwell Nov 15, 2025 Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share via Email Copy Link Link Copied LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 12: Eddie Murphy attends Netflix's "Being Eddie" premiere at Netflix Tudum Theater on November 12, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Presley Ann/Getty Images for Netflix) Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share via Email Copy Link Link Copied Ask any Eddie Murphy fan and they’ll tell you his best dramatic role was Jimmy Ealy in the 2006 film adaptation of “Dreamgirls.” The performance earned Murphy his first Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor, an award many predicted he would easily win. But Oscar night 2007 didn’t go Murphy’s way. When presenter Rachel Weisz revealed Alan Arkin had won for “Little Miss Sunshine” and not Murphy, the 64-year-old comedian seethed. Not because he didn’t win the award, but because he got dressed up to take home nothing. The revelation comes during “Being Eddie,” the revealing documentary about the 64-year-old comedian’s life, career and more. Murphy, who won a Golden Globe, a Screen Actors Guild Award and a Critics’ Choice Award for his performance, doesn’t feel bad about losing acting’s most prestigious award. “Not winning the Oscar or not winning anything is not the mindf–k for me,” Murphy says in the doc. “The mindf–k for me is that I get dressed and come to the thing, ’cause I would usually not go to award shows.” He added, “That’s… whenever I lose, I’m like, ‘These motherf–kers made me come all the way down.’ I could have f–king lost at home. I’m all in the f–king tuxedo. What a… a waste of time. I’m never, like, ‘Oh, I didn’t win.’ I’m like, ‘Hey, make me come down here for nothing?’ “ “It’s always wonderful to win stuff, but if I don’t win, I don’t give a f–k,” he adds. “I still come home, and it’s… I’m still Eddie in the morning.” The night wasn’t a complete loss for the “Dreamgirls” cast. Jennifer Hudson won for Best Supporting Actress, becoming the third Black woman to win the award. Since Hudson’s win, Mo’Nique, Octavia Spencer, Lupita Nyong’o, Viola Davis, Regina King, Ariana DeBose, Da’Vine Joy Randolph and Zoe Saldana have also taken home the honor. Murphy has a history of speaking his mind about the Academy Awards. At the 1988 ceremony , he spoke out about the lack of recognition for Black people in the motion picture industry. “I’ll probably never win an Oscar for saying this, but hey, I gotta say it,” Murphy told the audience. “Actually, I might not be in any trouble because the way it’s going every 20 years we get one, so we ain’t due until … 2004, so by that time all this will have blown over.” The irony of Murphy’s statement on that night? Jamie Foxx would win the Oscar for Best Actor for his performance in “Ray” in 2005. “I just want you to know I’m going to give this award,” he told the audience while recalling a conversation with his agent. “But Black people will not ride the caboose of society, and we will not bring up the rear anymore.
