Based out of Los Angeles, California, Brad lives close enough to the stars but is too busy to find out where exactly they live. Brad is fairly certain he's seen Paul Stanley twice in a grocery store, but was too afraid to ask. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap ​​​​​In a relatively short period of time, Apple TV has established itself as a streamer with quality original programming . From the feel-good comedy Ted Lasso to the sci-fi dark mystery Severance , Apple TV covers the spectrum of tastes. The same can be said for their varied offering of crime shows. From broadly comedic whodunits to slow-burning thrillers with high stakes, Apple TV has a number of crime shows to satisfy fans of the genre. The following list covers eight of the best crime shows on Apple TV , each featuring enough murder, destruction, or robberies to keep a precinct of hardened detectives busy for the next year. 8 'Dope Thief' (2025) Brian Tyree Henry as Ray with Wagner Moura as Manny as they reel back in shock in Dope Thief. Image via Apple TV+ In Dope Thief , two friends, Ray ( Brian Tyree Henry ) and Manny ( Wagner Moura ), pose as DEA agents to rob drug houses. The plan seems like an easy enough con that won’t trace back to them, but the pair manages to draw attention from both sides of the law. In over their heads and with no one to trust, Ray and Manny will have to act carefully if they hope to survive an ordeal of their own creation. Dope Thief is beautifully shot, with cinematic visuals that make the series look more like a film than a television series. Henry and Moura’s performances are the driving force of Dope Thief , and their struggle to remain loyal to one another despite the challenges they face elevates the series past a standard crime show. Those viewers looking for a fast-paced series probably won’t find it in Dope Thief , but an audience looking for strong character work will enjoy the eight episodes. 7 'The Afterparty' (2022–2023) Ben Schwartz and Sam Richardson in The Afterparty Image via Apple TV+ The after-party of a high school reunion becomes a crime scene in the Apple murder mystery comedy The Afterparty . Pop star Xavier ( Dave Franco ) went from host to corpse in a matter of hours, and while the guests get their stories straight, the overzealous Detective Danner ( Tiffany Haddish ) sees this as a case that could make her career. Danner begins taking statements from the possible suspects, and although their stories are wildly different, a bigger picture leading to the culprit starts to form. The Afterparty is the perfect farcical murder mystery comedy ideal for fans of movies like Clue . The format of the series, where each episode is a different person’s perspective of the night’s events, avoids the trap of becoming repetitive by hiding enough clues in a story told by its reliably unreliable narrator. Each season of The Afterparty focuses on a new case with a few returning characters, but each cast is packed with comedic talent such as Sam Richardson , Zach Woods , and Ilana Glazer , making sure the improvisational-sounding flow of the comedy is consistently smooth and sharp. 6 'Smoke' (2025–Current) 'Dave Gudsen looking intently to his left in Smoke. Image via Apple TV+ Smoke follows police detective Michelle Calderone ( Jurnee Smollett ) and arson investigator Dave Gudsen ( Taron Egerton ) as they attempt to track down two serial arsonists. Gudsen balks at having Calderone assigned to his case, but soon, a mutual respect grows between the two. However, each has personal demons that factor into their investigation — demons that could likely put them on opposite sides as more details come to light. The point of view of our arsonists, the horrific damage they cause, and the enjoyment they receive from it leads to some truly creepy moments that will stick in the mind for days afterward. Egerton and Smollett play off one another well, and as their relationship continues to change over the nine episodes, we see the two investigators wordlessly switch tactics with one another, making for a compelling watch. When the plot twists in Smoke land, they drastically impact the story and guarantee the “Next Episode’ button is getting pressed. ​​​​​​​​ 5 'Presumed Innocent' (2024–Current) Rusty is being led away in handcuffs in court with Raymond following in Presumed Innocent. Image via Apple TV+ The murder of an assistant prosecuting attorney becomes an even bigger scandal when the Chief Deputy Prosecutor is named the prime suspect. Presumed Innocent follows Rusty Sabich ( Jake Gyllenhaal ) as he is arrested and tried for the murder of his colleague, Carolyn Polhemus ( Renate Reinsve ), with whom he was having an affair. As the court case drags shameful secrets into the light, Rusty will find it increasingly difficult to prove his innocence. Even for those familiar with the original novel of the same name by Scott Turow or the 1990 film adaptation starring Harrison Ford , the TV version of Presumed Innocent will offer new plot twists to keep viewers engaged. Gyllenhaal shines as a man grappling with guilt about his involvement with the victim , but there’s no weak link in the phenomenal cast that includes Ruth Negga as his wife, Barbara, and Bill Camp as his former boss-turned-legal counsel, Raymond Horgan. The second season of Presumed Innocent will shift the series into an anthology format with a new case to follow, but anyone looking for a quick binge will receive a complete story with Season 1. ​​​​​​ ​​​​​​ 4 'Bad Monkey' (2024–Current) Vince Vaughn sitting in a beach chair with a drink in Bad Monkey Episode 1. Image via Apple TV+ In Bad Monkey , Andrew Yancy ( Vince Vaughn ) was a great police detective who became a fairly apathetic health inspector after an altercation that put him in hot water. The arrival of a severed arm pulls Yancy back into some unofficial police work, and the fast-talking health inspector finds himself the target of some dangerous and increasingly desperate individuals. In the off chance Yancy can keep his personal life under control, he has a fighting chance of repairing his professional life if he can avoid getting killed in the process. Based on the novel of the same name by Carl Hiaasen, Bad Monkey allows its characters to be playful and get lost in banter while never losing sight of the murder mystery or the stakes of the case. Bad Monkey is the best balance of comedy and crime currently on Apple TV , and with a lead like Vaughn, who can keep one foot in both genres easily, it's a series that lends itself to substantial longevity on the streamer. The second season of Bad Monkey promises to give Yancy new co-stars to tangle with , which is one more reason to be excited for the return of the likable series. 3 'Your Friends & Neighbors' (2025–Current) A man goes from the envy of his upper-class community to the person breaking into their homes in Your Friends & Neighbors . Andrew “Coop” Cooper ( Jon Hamm ) is still emotionally reeling after the divorce from his wife, Mel ( Amanda Peet ), when he loses his job as a prominent hedge fund manager. Jaded from his recent failures and disillusioned by the wealth he sees around him, Coop begins to steal from the people he once thought of as friends. However, entering their homes allows Coop access to more than their valuables — he also discovers secrets they would kill to protect. Your Friends & Neighbors wisely relied on the charm and dry comedic ability of Hamm in the early stages of its story, but the series slowly built an interesting world around him. By the end of Season 1, many of the supporting characters were fully fleshed out into people who could carry side plots, which will only stand to make the show better. The end of Season 1 left many questions about how Coop moves forward with his life in light of major decisions, so it will be intriguing to see what his next steps are and how they impact his family, friends… and neighbors for Season 2. 2 'Criminal Record' (2024–Current) Cush Jumbo and Peter Capaldi standing beside each other in Criminal Record Image via Apple TV+ New details about an old murder case pit two detectives against one another in Criminal Record . An anonymous phone call leads Detective Sergeant June Lenker ( Cush Jumbo ) to believe an innocent man might be in jail for a murder he didn’t commit. June’s attempts to uncover the truth are blocked by Detective Chief Inspector Daniel Hegarty ( Peter Capaldi ), who believes firmly that the case in question should remain closed. When neither detective backs down, a professional disagreement quickly becomes personal. Criminal Record is one of Apple TV’s best crime offerings, loaded with the type of expertly laid out plot twists and tense drama that are the recipe for addictive television. Capaldi and Jumbo create a unique antagonistic chemistry that puts a fresh spin on a procedural mystery thriller, where the more they outmaneuver one another, the deeper their respect and will to succeed grow. With a confirmed second season of Criminal Record on the way, now is a great time to catch up before June and Daniel are back on the case. ​​​​​​​ 1 'Black Bird' (2022) James in on a payphone in prison in Black Bird. Image via Apple TV+ In the intense and thrilling miniseries Black Bird , Jimmy (Taron Egerton) is a small-time crook given a once-in-a-lifetime chance to commute his 10-year sentence. The prize is great, and so is the challenge: Jimmy must befriend fellow inmate Larry Hall ( Paul Walter Hauser ) with the goal of getting a confession about suspected murders. Larry is distrustful, guards are dangerous, and Jimmy doesn’t have much time before the offer expires. Egerton takes Jimmy from arrogant to honorable with no false moments, and Hauser rightfully won an Emmy by making Larry one of the most unnerving characters on television that year. There are moments of Black Bird that become so uncomfortably tense that it’s not uncommon to feel tired after watching an episode . That’s said as the highest form of compliment, because the story continues to raise the stakes scene by scene via a masterful combination of writing and acting, making Black Bird the easiest recommendation for fans of any genre. The Duchess of Sussex , 44, is said to have been 'swamped with offers' for her return to the limelight, and will be playing herself in the film Close Personal Friends, with filming taking place in Pasadena in LA. But before she married Prince Harry and joined the royal family , Meghan's acting career looked very different - consisting mainly of bit parts and cameos in largely forgettable and poorly reviewed movies - and she was not nearly so in demand. Before making her name as Rachel Zane in the TV show Suits, Meghan secured minor Hollywood roles in Horrible Bosses (2011) and Remember Me (2010) - where she was typecast as a 'cute' or 'hot girl', with only seconds of screentime . Often, her cameo and pilot roles, such as her brief appearance kissing Russell Brand in Get Him To The Greek (2010) and The Boys And Girls Guide To Getting Down (2011), never actually ended up making the final cut. As a result, the now-Duchess was forced to resort to a series of raunchy roles - and was seen parading around in sexy negligee for the majority of her feature in 2012's Random Encounters - not to mention her explicit scene in the 90210 TV series . Critics, meanwhile, were less than impressed with the final results, even warning viewers that Meghan's 2006 film Deceit would 'bore them to death'. When she finally did score leading roles towards the end of her acting career, Meghan was mainly seen in repetitive and unchallenging Hallmark Movies, receiving mixed reviews at best. The mother-of-two previously told how she would get plenty of auditions but was regularly rejected by directors - which was a 'lot to chip away at your self-esteem'. Here, we give a rundown of all Meghan's film roles before meeting Prince Harry - most of which you probably won't have heard of... A Lot Like Love (2005) Meghan made her film debut in 2005, playing Natalie, the 'Hot Girl' in A Lot Like Love Meghan, then aged 24 and an unknown actress, made her big screen debut alongside Hollywood heartthrob Ashton Kutcher in the 2005 film called A Lot Like Love , where she was famously credited as 'Hot Girl.' The Duchess' very first film role was a total flop at the box office but Meghan herself, wearing a bright pink top, was only on screen for 31 seconds, and saw her attempting to flirt with Kutcher's internet entrepreneur character Oliver Martin on a flight. But she was left stunned when Oliver showed no interest because of his complicated on-off relationship with photographer Emily Friehl, Alias actress Amanda Peet. And she ended up being chatted up by business partner Jetter played by actor Kal Penn instead, who was sat across the aisle. Although she introduced herself as Natalie, she only appeared in the credits as 'Hot Girl.' The film was like an American version of One Day, where a couple met regularly over a seven-year period before falling in love. The moment was featured in Harry and Meghan's Netflix docu-series as they discussed Meghan's film career. The film received mixed reviews and a score of 40 per cent on Rotten Tomatoes, while one review in the Observer called it 'neither bad nor good enough to be anything other than utterly forgettable'. Deceit (2006) Meghan played Gwen in 2006's Deceit, again another small role for the budding actress In her second film role, Meghan again landed only a small part, playing a girl-next-door called Gwen, again appearing only in one scene. Over the kitchen table, Meghan's characeter dispensed unwanted advice to a friend caught up in a murder mystery. Her handy advice included lines such as: 'You're an investigative journalist; do what you do best - investigate her' The psychological thriller, released in 2006, followed a young man returning home after his father's death and falling in love with his best friend's wife. It explored attraction, violence, and deception. Meghan played Gwen in one scene in the film, a friend of the protagonist who offered advice to the main character. Director Matthew Cole Weiss previously revealed he'd met Prince Harry, who told him he had watched the film. The film has poor reviews online, scoring just 4.5/10 on IMDB, with viewers saying it has 'weak acting,' 'no characters' adding it will 'bore you to death'. Remember Me (2010) The Duchess did score some Hollywood roles in her film acting career, starring in Remember Me alongside Robert Pattinson In Remember Me, starring Robert Pattinson and Emilie de Ravin, Meghan had a small role as a bartender, who was aptly named Megan. She briefly interacted with Pattinson's character and only had one, three-word line: 'Do not speak', when she told his friend not to chat with her. On working with the Twilight star, Meghan recalled: 'He's a really lovely guy and a really great example to be able to watch someone who is young, who's stardom has really taken over his live in such a huge way, and yet he's still gracious, humble and cool. I think that is really endearing.' This movie marked Robert Pattinson's departure from his Twilight fame, so it would be easy to forget that a future star had a small role in the same production as well. The movie follows the story of Tyler Hawkins, who falls in love with Amy, played by Emilie de Ravin, but dies in the Twin Towers on 9/11/2001. The rom com was a financial success, grossing $56million worldwide. However, it fared less well with critics, only scoring 26 per cent on Rotten Tomatoes. The twist at the end of the show - that Pattinson's character is in his father's office in the World Trade Centre when the 9/11 attacks take place - was branded 'shockingly offensive' by Rolling Stone, and 'exploitative' by other reviewers. Meghan's real life ex-husband Trevor Engelson, was one of the film's producers, and the pair tied the knot a year later, during a party-filled celebration in Jamaica in 2011. They eventually divorced in 2014, with Meghan being linked to several men during her single years before she met now-husband Prince Harry in 2016. Get Him To The Greek (2010) Meghan Markle played Tatiana in comedy Get Him To The Greek, in which she's seen kissing comedian Russell Brand Meghan Markle played Tatiana in comedy Get Him To The Greek, in which she's seen kissing comedian Russell Brand. She reportedly had a 40-second role as a girl in a strapless metallic dress and snogged Brand's character. However, Meghan was never given a credit in the film and the scene never made it to the final cut. Is this really her? The film was not panned by critics and was even said to have had its 'moments' - though Meghan's role was too short to appear in any of them. Horrible Bosses (2011) Horrible Bosses continued the trend of Meghan playing bit parts in Hollywood dark comedies Horrible Bosses in 2011 saw Meghan star alongside Jennifer Aniston and Jason Sudeikis. However, it seemed to continue the trend of her playing bit parts in Hollywood dark comedies, again having only a short cameo. This situation you have going on, it's got to get tucked in.' The film followed nine friends who went their different ways after finishing college before reuniting at a rich friend's funeral. They find out that they will be eligible for a big inheritance if they stay at his mansion for five days. It bombed at the box office but paved the way for Markle to take on more serious roles. Keyes later told People Magazine that he had been 'slapped' by the 'future Queen' during filming. He explained: '[Meghan] said, 'I might improv an extra smack,' and I was like, 'smack away!' 'I knew she was going to put a little hand on it. She had some torque and rotation in the wrist.' 'It was one of her first acting gigs and she has [acting] chops, she had them back then. She was great on set. She was super cool and approachable. She was a class act.' Random Encounters (2013) Meghan had another racy role in Random Encounters, playing party girl Mindy Filmed over 18 days in 2010, the low budget romantic comedy was set in the showbusiness community in Los Angeles In Random Encounters, Meghan played Mindy, a party girl who brings home a different guy every night, and the best friend of singleton Laura, who strikes up a romance with Kevin, a man she met in a coffee shop. Filmed over 18 days in 2010, the low budget romantic comedy was set in the showbusiness community in Los Angeles. During the chick flick, which was made pre-Suits before being re-released, Mindy popped up in a host of revealing outfits including a sexy negligee before seducing a male co-star and sleeping with a cop who stopped her for a traffic offence. In one scene, Mindy could be seen showing her friend the ropes on 'the biggest dating site in LA'. She also revealed her top tips for catching a man's eye in a night club: 'Look like you're really bored and have a serious attitude problem.' When her frustrated single friend moaned that she is 'chasing a guy who doesn't insist,' Mindy replied: 'Oh honey, aren't we all.' 'It just goes to show, you just have to be in the right place at the right time. Sometimes, you only get one shot.' In one particularly racy scene Meghan was seen undressing actor Michael Rady as her character tried to make a move in a dimly-lit apartment. At other points in the film, Meghan flitted across the screen in flirty summer dresses and party frocks. Director Boris Undorf later spoke about Markle's can-do attitude while filming, reflecting: 'All the comforts of a bigger project weren't there. 'She was very much like, 'Yep, I got it. I know it's long hours, but I love doing it, and I'll do my best' to serve the film, not just myself.'' Co-star Abby Wathen (Laura) added: 'It was great to work with Meghan because she's a pro, and it's great to work with pros... It was lovely. We sat in my trailer and just giggled. She's just vivacious.' In 2018, the budget rom com was released in the UK for the first time - just two weeks before Meghan married Prince Harry. When Sparks Fly (2014) In 2014, Meghan finally landed her first major film role in Hallmark movie, When Sparks Fly Meghan's character Amy finds there's no place like how when she reunited with her high school sweetheart In 2014, Meghan finally landed a major film role, playing the lead role in the Hallmark movie, When Sparks Fly. She played Amy Peterson, a journalist who quits her small town for the big city of Chicago. She then returned to her hometown to write a human interest story about Independence Day weekend. Amy discovered that there's no place like home - and no boy like her high school sweetheart. Meghan said at the time: 'I wanted to do a romantic comedy. When the script came in, it was exactly the kind of project I wanted to be part of. 'It was light and easy and it was a departure from Rachel [Suits], who is so refined and polished. Amy Peterson is very opposite and closer to my true personality. 'It was fun to eat ribs and get barbecue sauce all over my face and run around in jeans all day.' Hallmark films all generally follow the same plot points, and while they make for comforting watching, are generally not considered 'challenging' acting roles. In 2021 alone, the channel made 41 Christmas films, with each film relatively low budget and without famous names. Anti-Social (2015) Meghan - then 35 - played American fashion model Kirsten who falls in love with Dee (Gregg Sulkin) in Anti-Social Following her relationship with Prince Harry, the film was re-released and re-edited to give Meghan a bigger role Set in England and filmed largely in Hungary, Anti-Social followed a successful street artist who was forced to jeopardise his future to help his criminal brother when gang rivalry escalates. The gangland war turned their lives upside down, bringing the attention of the police as well as other criminals. The low-budget British coming-of-age story was inspired by a number of real-life smash-and-grab raids across London from 2009 to 2013. Again, the Duchess was chosen to play the female lead and it even co-starred grime star Skepta. Meghan - then 35 - played American fashion model Kirsten who falls in love with Dee (Gregg Sulkin), a talented Banksy-esque street-artist who was sucked into crime. One of her lines included: 'I know you have had to climb a mountain to get away from this crap and see life for what it can be. You inspire me.' Following her relationship with Prince Harry, the film was re-released and re-edited to give Meghan a bigger role as bosses sought to capitalise on her new royal links. Originally, it had been shown at just 40 screens in the UK when it was released in 2015. Speaking of the decision to re-release it, Director Reg Traviss - who had dated Amy Winehouse before she died - said he wanted to 'delve deeper into one of the storylines with.. a shorter, more compact version of the original'. In the three-minute trailer, Meghan's character was shown modelling perfume, emerging from a shower and drinking champagne at a number of West End nightclubs. She was heard saying: 'I'm going to go and see my boyfriend, he's an artist. A street artist.' In a scene which showed shoot-outs in London, depicting Marcus and his cool friends getting pulled into a dangerous gang war, she said: 'I hate violence... I'm from a sleepy little beach town, I'm just not used to this.' Upon its release, the film generally received negative reviews, with one critic calling the film a 'painful slog'. In The Observer, critic Mark Kermode awarded it two stars, calling it an 'uninspiring crime caper' that 'sits awkwardly alongside dreary discussions of the politics of street art'. Dater's Handbook (2016) Meghan's final film role saw her play Cassandra Barber in 2016's Dater's Handbook Cass soon realised that there was no rule book to love, binned her manual and met the man of her dreams In Meghan's final film role before quitting the industry upon joining the Royal Family, she played another lead role for the Hallmark Channel, in 2016's Dater's Handbook. The romantic movie centred around Cassandra Barber, who realised she had a recurring habit of picking the wrong type of guy, turning to relationship expert, Dr. Susie, and her latest self-help book, The Dater's Handbook to help with her ailing love life. 'Of course I wanna get married,' Meghan's character Cass told her mother. 'I've got to change how I choose relationships.' She followed the advice in Dr. Susie's book to evaluate potential suitors, and was forced to choose between reliable George (Jonathan Scarfe) and fun-loving Robert (Kristoffer Polaha). Cass soon realised that there was no rule book to love, binned her manual and met the man of her dreams. Little did Meghan know that six months later she'd meet her real-life prince. Successful career women, both Cassandra and Meghan were set up with their dream suitor by a mutual pal, bonding on and off-screen with their respective suitors over their shared love of animals and the great outdoors. Additionally, Meghan and her character were whisked away on sporty dates by their suitors - while Cass' mother joined the pair at a concert in the movie, Harry flew Meghan's mother Doria to the Invictus Games in Toronto in real life. Many joked at the time of the movie's release that while the character she played on screen had been unlucky in love, Meghan's real love life was very different. During the film's press tour, Meghan said: 'At the end of the day, when it comes down to finding the person that you're right for, that's not the person you're going to play games with. 'I think following her heart has really ended up proving to work out well for Cass, and I think for a lot of women watching this, I would give them that same advice.' The film, a classic Hallmark movie, was branded 'predictable and simple' by critics. On IMDB, one reviewer even said: 'The story was silly, the acting was below average, and the actors had no chemistry.' I’m not a conventional beauty’ The actor speaks to Dazed about being scared of ageing, why she hated her Botox lip flip, and her latest role as a US ambassador for Miu Miu Beauty’s Miutine Share Link copied ✔️ November 3, 2025 Beauty Beauty Feature Text Laura Pitcher Read More Music 7 musicians who had their secret identities exposed Art & Photography Candid photos from a Paris strip club locker room Art & Photography These photos trace a diasporic archive of transness In photos: The beauty evolution of Chloë Sevigny Gallery / 20 images Miu Miu uses the name Miutine, their irreverent fragrance, as an adjective to describe an individual whose spirit is unyielding and unconstrained. “One who navigates life on their own terms…effortlessly,” the brand says. “They do not always show up on time... But when they arrive… You notice.” Fittingly, as Miu Miu Beauty’s new ambassador, Chloë Sevigny did in fact show up to our call late – but she did so with noticeable conviction. Sevigny joins tennis champion Coco Gauff and model Paloma Elsesser as one of the three new US Miu Miu Beauty ambassadors, with a digital campaign brought to life by artist-filmmaker Petra Collins. The first thing Sevigny did when she heard that she’d been chosen as the US ambassador of the brand was tell her mum. “She seems the most pleased and proud of me more than anyone else in my life,” she says. “And she also knows my longstanding relationship with Miuccia, and how much I respect and value her as a businesswoman and creative type.” And it’s true – Sevigny has long been (or as she puts it, has “forever” been ) a Miu Miu girl. She’s been mu(i)se for Miuccia Prada since the 90s, when she walked the runway as an angsty teenager wearing one of the Spring 1996 ready-to-wear crop tops, and even directed a film for the brand in 2017 . Even when she speaks about Miuccia, she gushes. “I just find her so inspiring; so for her to want me to be one of the faces of the fragrance was such an honour,” says Sevigny. “She’s celebrated me for almost 30 years now, and just having her support throughout my career has meant so much to me.” Petra Collins / Miu Miu Sevigny, Gauff and Elsesser join the global face of the fragrance, Emma Corrin , to paint a multifaceted picture of what the spirit of Miutine looks like: youthful in spirit and unconventional. “This is a celebration of women who exist on their own terms. Women who know the rules – and quietly undo them,” says Petra Collins. And there’s perhaps no greater example of someone who has built a career on being unabashedly themselves, staying true to their tastes and sensibilities, than Sevigny. She’s one of the rare celebrities whose years spent in the industry haven’t seemed at all to impact her ability to have an unfiltered (and often hilarious) conversation. Dazed caught up with Sevigny ahead of the launch to talk more about rebellion, building an unconventional career, pouting like Lily Rose Depp , and finding ageing “terrifying”. Congrats on being named one of the US ambassadors of Miu Miu Beauty! You’ve obviously had such a long-standing relationship with Miu Miu. Why do you think you’re so aligned? Chloë Sevigny: There’s a kookiness, perhaps, or a playfulness that I inhabit that aligns with the brand. People associate me with that; I’m very irreverent. I don’t want to say quirky, but there’s a certain quirk to me. I’m not a conventional beauty. I’m not a conventional actress. I’m not a conventional celebrity or personality. That’s a lot of the things that Miu Miu leans into, and our strengths align. So what’s been your favourite moment in or with Miu Miu? Chloë Sevigny: Every one kind of surpasses the last, but there was a show that I walked with Gwendolyn Christie and Uma Thurman. There were a group of actresses involved in that show, and I love the fact that they have always celebrated actresses. And, of course, being an actress myself, I just think it was cool to have us all walking the runway because we’re not models. There’s something very freeing about celebrating these more unconventional beauties. I felt very proud to be a part of that show. Tell me more about ‘Miutine’. Where do you like to wear it? Chloë Sevigny: I like to spray it on my wrists and then dab it around with my natural oils. And it’s very long-lasting, you don’t have to use a lot, which I think is rare in a fragrance these days. It’s very hard to find. I usually spray it on my wrists and then behind my ears on top of my head, and then sometimes on whatever garments I’m wearing. It’s been a couple of years since we’ve caught up with you at Dazed Beauty. Is there something new that you’ve added to your beauty routine since then? Chloë Sevigny: I was never into this lip liner thing, but I have been plumping up my lips with a little lip liner. Lily Rose Depp, to me, is like a pretty doll version of Christina Ricci. I’m just so obsessed with her and her make-up artist, Nina Park. I want to have lips, and I’m also 50, so I’m not doing injections and stuff. For me, lip liner is a fun way to kind of plump ‘em up when you’re going out, just to feel a little sassy. I tried doing a little Botox lip flip once, and I went to the doctor the next day, like, ‘I can’t handle this. This makes me feel insane. Make it stop right now.’ I couldn’t even suck a straw. I’m the worst contender for that kind of thing, so the lip liner is a really good sneaky alternative. Yeah, I’ve seen on TikTok some people can’t drink from a straw with that. Chloë Sevigny: Oh my God. I couldn’t even suck a straw! It was terrifying. I was like, ‘How do people do this?’ And she’s like, ‘It’ll go away eventually’. It made me feel paranoid and insane. Aside from your lip liner, what are three products that you don’t leave the house without? Chloë Sevigny: I can’t leave the house without a comb or a brush. I have an OCD about brushing both my eyebrows and the hair on my head, which is really weird and gross. I obviously try to do it in private areas like bathrooms, but I have a thing about it. I have this little comb in my bag and then a little hair brush from Jenna Perry, my colourist, who makes these pocket brushes that flip open. It’s purple. It has her initials on it, and then you pop out. The brush also has a mirror. It’s very helpful. Then I can’t really leave my house without Dr Paw Paw Balm. I’m an obsessive hand washer, so then my hands get dry and I need something to rub on my fingertips and my cuticles. That is my favourite. The third thing would be Weleda Skin Food, which is to make my cheeks a little more dewy and also for my hands. I was so staunchly against Hollywood that I would’ve told my 19-year-old self to just be more open to more commercial work, more comedic work. I was very scared. I didn’t think I was funny. And now I get to do a lot of comedy ‘Miutine’ has been described as ‘irreverent’ and ‘unconventional’. Do you consider yourself a rebellious person? Chloë Sevigny: I think rebellion is something that I’ve always been attracted to; people who exist outside of the norm and aren’t interested in bowing to convention, who would rather break moulds and introduce new ways of seeing things. Or even introducing conversations that people aren’t necessarily having. That can be through film, fashion and art, however, especially with the filmmakers that I’ve been drawn to, from Kids to Boys Don’t Cry to even all of my work with Ryan Murphy. It’s just making people have uncomfortable conversations that can hopefully help propel society forward. I feel like those kinds of things always come out of a more rebellious nature. It’s actually been 30 years this year since Kids first came out. What would you tell your 19-year-old self now? Chloë Sevigny: I was very selective. Now, things have changed, but in the 90s, it was like you were either indie or you weren’t. I had a very staunch commitment to being indie and not Hollywood. Now, I think there’s more fluidity, and you can kind of do both. I mean, I probably could have gotten away with it. There are women now who have come out on the other side, like Michelle Williams or Kirsten Dunst, and they navigated both. I was so staunchly against Hollywood that I would’ve told my 19-year-old self to just be more open to more commercial work, more comedic work. I was very scared. I didn’t think I was funny. And now I get to do a lot of comedy. But if I had been open to doing more comedies early, maybe I would have had a different career path. I don’t know. How has your relationship to beauty, or overall beauty philosophy, changed over the years? Chloë Sevigny: I feel like it’s been pretty consistent. I feel like I’ve always tried to play up my strengths: my eyelashes, my hair and dressing for my legs, or whatever. I know what works for me, and I think I leaned into the red lip for so many years because I felt like it would draw people’s eyes to my lips and not my nose. Just ways of finding beauty tricks to accentuate whatever you already like about yourself, instead of focusing on things you don’t. That’s something I still try to do, but now I’m 50 and ageing is really terrifying. Middle age is a really weird place to be in. I’m still trying to figure out how to navigate that and find confidence in that – to not be so scared of it. Speaking of beauty tricks, do you have any for us all? Chloë Sevigny: I mean, other than going to my dermatologist for a very expensive PRP? They are so boring: if I have a big event, I try not to drink alcohol for a few days before just to be really hydrated. Dehydration is really from the inside out. I’m also very into doing an ice bath before an event for my face. I don’t even know if that really works. But I love under-eye patches and keep those in the fridge. Even if it doesn’t work, it makes you feel like it goes. I also have a little Ziip , a microcurrent device, that’s also expensive, so now I feel like such a cow just naming all of these expensive devices. But also just moving your body around and jumping up and down a bunch. If it gets you to emotionally feel better, you’re going to look better. That can help with all of that: getting your nerves fired up. By Hannah Jackson November 18, 2025 Jim Smeal/Getty Images Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story Today marks 51 years of Chloë Sevigny . The actor has been on the scene for more than half her life, earning her It-girl distinction in a sprawling seven-page article in The New Yorker in 1994. While Sevigny cut her teeth in film with Kids, her singular sense of style is not to be overlooked. Sevigny knows no bounds when it comes to fashion. She offered a casual take on menswear at the 1999 Academy Awards nominees’ luncheon, donning a pair of gray shorts and a long, loose necktie. But, on the other end of the spectrum, she isn’t afraid to lean into the sex appeal, like when she wore a spring 2004 Louis Vuitton cutout dress by Marc Jacobs to play blackjack at Copacabana. These days, Sevigny continues to live up to the It-girl name, strolling down the street in over-the-top Prada coats and variations on a classic ballet flat in lace-up ECCOs. And while she’s no stranger to the likes of Chanel Haute couture, Miu Miu (which she’s walked the runway for multiple times), and Saint Laurent (she currently is the face of a larger-than-life ad campaign), she also champions younger brands like Christopher John Rogers and Simone Rocha. This past year alone, she’s championed the emerging shoe brand Jude, and pushed the envelope in a bubble-skirted Saint Laurent dress with a lace catsuit beneath. Between her unmatched street style and risk-taking red carpet looks, Chloë Sevigny is exercising her lifelong commitment to serving. Here are their November premieres: Under The Silver Lake November 7 David Robert Mitchell’s Under the Silver Lake is a black comedy thriller that effortlessly blends neo-noir, surrealism, and pop-culture paranoia into a puzzle-box for obsessive film viewers. Featuring Andrew Garfield as a slacker drifting through Los Angeles, the film follows young and disenchanted Sam who meets a mysterious woman swimming in his building’s pool one night. When she suddenly vanishes the next morning, Sam embarks on a surreal quest across Los Angeles to decode the secret behind her disappearance. The film spirals into conspiracies, codes, and secret societies hidden beneath the city’s surface, satirizing millennial aimlessness and Los Angeles’s glossy facades while critiquing Hollywood’s fantasies and the objectification they sustain. Rich with hidden codes, backwards messages, and Easter eggs, the film has garnered a devoted cult following. It premiered at Cannes to divisive but passionate responses. Magic Farm November 14 Amalia Ulman’s sharp comedy Magic Farm examines the fraught relationship between American media and Latin American subjects through a lens of absurdist satire. This playful yet pointed critique follows a misguided American documentary crew working for an edgy media company who travel to rural Argentina to profile a local musician but end up in the wrong small town entirely. As they collaborate with locals to fabricate a viral trend, unexpected connections blossom while a pervasive environmental crisis looms unacknowledged in the background. Beneath the absurdity, the film carries a serious environmental and public health critique about herbicide contamination, illness, and water toxicity in the farming region. With a jagged, energetic tone that combines performances, mini-setups, visual experiments, and improvisation, the film employs fisheye lenses and dog-mounted GoPro shots with sharp color saturation. Amalia Ulman plays Elena, the translator stuck between cultures, with Chloë Sevigny adding sharp star power as the crew’s driven director. The film premiered at Sundance and screened at Berlin. Another Round November 21 Thomas Vinterberg’s Academy Award-winning Another Round follows four stagnant high school teachers who decide to test out a theory that maintaining a constant level of intoxication will improve their overall lives. Anchored by Mads Mikkelsen’s remarkable performance that shifts from muted despair to flashes of joy, the film culminates in one of the most celebrated dance sequences in recent cinema. Balancing humor and heartbreak, Vinterberg refuses easy moral lessons about alcohol or control. As the experiment spirals out of control and the characters are forced to confront the limits of escape, the film offers a meditation on control versus release in a society obsessed with order and measurement. The film won the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film and played at TIFF and San Sebastian. Movies Julia Roberts’ Massive Pay for New Movie That Bombed Revealed October 29, 2025 By Maggie Dela Paz Following After the Hunt ‘s underwhelming box office performance, Academy Award winner Julia Roberts ‘ salary for the Luca Guadagnino -led drama was revealed in a new report discussing the box office fallout of recently released adult upscale movies. The college-set psychological thriller movie only earned a total gross of 6 million at the box office against a reported budget of around $70-80 million. Besides its disappointing theatrical run, it also didn’t perform well among critics and audiences alike. Since its world premiere at the 2025 Venice International Festival, the movie has received a Tomatometer rating of 38% on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 193 reviews. How much was Julia Roberts’ salary for After the Hunt? According to Deadline, Roberts was reportedly paid a $20 million salary for her role as Alma Imhoff, who is described as a well-liked professor at Yale University. In the movie, her character gets caught in the middle of a scandal concerning her star student and close colleague. Roberts will next be seen in a brand new thriller movie, Panic Carefully, with Elizabeth Olsen and Eddie Redmayne. “The film is a gripping psychological drama about a college professor who finds herself at a personal and professional crossroads when a star student levels an accusation against one of her colleagues, and a dark secret from her own past threatens to come into the light,” reads the official synopsis. Guadagnino directed After the Hunt from a screenplay written by Nora Garrett. The ensemble cast also included Andrew Garfield , Ayo Edebiri , Michael Stuhlbarg, Chloë Sevigny, Lío Mehiel, Thaddea Graham, Ariyan Kassam, Will Price, Christine Dye, and Burgess Byrd. It was executive produced by Garrett, Karen Lunder, Justin Wilkes, and Alice Dawson, with Guadagnino, Brian Grazer, Jeb Brody, and Allan Mandelbaum serving as producers. Subscribe to Marketing Daily hotels Musician Orville Peck Loses His Mask In Latest Ad From W Hotels by Danielle Oster , October 28, 2025 Country musician Orville Peck is seldom seen without his signature Lone Ranger-esque mask. So it was a pretty big deal when he lost it while on tour. Peck recounts the ordeal for the latest installment in Marriott International luxury hotel brand W Hotels’ “Hotel Tales” series, entitled “ The Masked Chase .” He relates that he was reaching for the mask backstage before a show, when he realized he left it on his laundry bag in his room. The story concludes with a W Insider (the brand’s name for its dedicated concierge service) tracking down the mask and delivering it to Peck’s room, on a silver platter, allowing Peck to retrieve it before showtime. The new campaign was shot in and around the recently renovated W Austin. In addition to the 47-second “Hotel Tales” installment, there’s also a 15-second edit, and four 6-second versions, as well as four behind-the-scenes videos, an upcoming trailer, and additional social media assets. Peck’s spot follows appearances by actress Chloë Sevigny and multidisciplinary artist Miranda Makaroff . The approach, featuring unexpected, ostensibly true stories from cultural celebrities, has proven successful. Trending Desk / etimes.in / Nov 09, 2025, 05:30 IST Share AA + Text Size Small Medium Large Vogue's December cover featuring Timothée Chalamet has sparked debate and accusations of AI generation due to its ethereal, cosmic aesthetic. The image, intended to symbolize exploration, instead drew comparisons to AI art and "galaxy-print leggings. Source: Instagram/@tchalamet It’s not every day that Vogue, the so-called fashion bible, stirs an identity crisis. But its December issue has done just that. Standing in brown leather boots, a cream topcoat and floral embroidered jeans by Celine, Timothée Chalamet appears to hover over a blue planet, surrounded by a cosmic haze. The image, shot by Annie Leibovitz, was meant to be ethereal. Instead, it’s become a flashpoint, sparking memes, mockery, and even suspicion that it might have been conjured by AI. The timing couldn’t be thornier. Vogue, long the unshakable authority of fashion publishing, is in transition. Just this week, Teen Vogue was folded into its parent site, and a new head of editorial content, Chloé Malle, stepped into the role once synonymous with Anna Wintour’s untouchable reign. Change, as it turns out, doesn’t come quietly, especially to an institution built on consistency. Chalamet’s cover, cosmic and melancholic, might have been intended as a metaphor for exploration, his zeal to succeed to be counted among the greats- a dream that he has been very open about. But to many, it simply looked off. Online, users compared it to “galaxy-print leggings” and AI-generated fan art. One user wrote on X, "Please somebody tell me this isn’t a real. This ChatGPT looking cover of Timothee Chalamet cannot be the December issue of American Vogue. What is going on over there?" Another wrote, "As a designer…this is crazy & not in a good way lol." However a third had some different opinion. They wrote, "I actually applaud the new EIC of Vogue for stepping away from the boring, repetitive covers they’ve had for a while now. I don’t think this is perfect, but it’s exciting to see something different!" Even Bones and All co-star Chloë Sevigny chimed in, fanning the flames of debate. Yet, ironically, as it turns out the universe wasn’t entirely artificial. The image incorporated actual NASA visuals, the Emission Nebula and O6.5 Star, provided by the Hubble Telescope Heritage Team. By Aaron Royce November 17, 2025 Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story Clémence Polès, Myriam Ben Salah, Arsh Raziuddin, Zohar Benjelloun, Rama Duwaji, Aminah Al Huqail, Farah Al Qasimi Photo by: Janna Tew On Sunday afternoon, a thoroughly modern approach to parenthood and child-like wonder both came out to play at the first-ever Artists & Mothers Gala. The invite even came with an instruction to wear whatever you please, as opposed to a traditional formal dress code—much to everyone’s delight. The non-profit was launched a little over a year ago in a bid to help artists achieve balance between their professional and personal lives. Held at the WSA building downtown, the event raised funds towards nine month-long $25,000 grants to apply towards childcare for toddlers aged three and below. “This felt like a way to start quickly—to be grassroots, to mobilize our network, and put it right back into the mission, which is to support artists with childcare,” co-founder Julia Trotta told Vogue . “We didn’t even know if we’d be able to fund one grant, and in the first year, we funded four.” Indeed, though Artists & Mothers is in its infancy, the collective force of its board and host committee—which includes Chloë Sevigny—drew a supportive crowd. During the afternoon, kids and their parents indulged in creative and colorful activities. There was an ivy-covered backdrop by Farah Al Qasimi for sweet family photos, a lounge filled with beanbags by artist Maia Ruth Lee and videos by Aki Goto, and a massive tile-covered installation by Ei Arakawa prompting everyone to “please draw freely”—which many did, creating a colorful collage filled with jungle animals, mermaids, and modernist scribbles. An on-site gift shop also held delights sure to keep a smile on faces after home-time, including graphic Gauchere T-shirts, beanies, tote bags, and nylon patchwork dolls by Abby Lloyd. Régime des Fleurs perfumer Alia Raza, whose travel-sized fragrances everyone received as a parting gift alongside handprint-shaped sugar cookies, felt impassioned by the non-profit’s goal. “There’s still this [unspoken] choice for women which is, ‘do you want to have a full-throttle career, or do you want to be a mom?’ In New York, many women do both—but in the rest of the country and the rest of the world, a lot of women still feel like it’s something they have to choose between. If you do choose to do both, it’s really hard. I hope that when I’m a parent, there will be organizations like this around that will help.” As for that optional dress code? Its freedom allowed guests including Rama Duwaji, Liana Satenstein, Legacy Russell, Rachel Chandler, and Camille Henrot to prioritize individuality. The resulting mix was a scene that felt cool yet easygoing, with no shortage of wide-legged jeans, maxi skirts, and colorful knits paired with chunky boots, sneakers, and convenient crossbody bags that ranged from Adidas and Acne to Stella McCartney and Staud. The actress had her breakthroughs in Mystic Pizza in 1988 and Steel Magnolias in 1989. She shot to fame with her work in the romantic comedies Pretty Woman, My Best Friend's Wedding, Notting Hill, and Runaway Bride. One of the most famous examples is Angelina Jolie, whose blended family has always been central to her public life. Unlike True Detective , which explores crime with some supernatural undertones, The Last Frontier grounds its premise in government conspiracies. At the center of it all is U.S. Marshal Frank Remnick ( Jason Clarke ), who is tasked with overseeing law and order in his remote, tight-knit community. However, things take a turn when a prisoner transport airplane crashes on the tundra. The show's official logline explains: "Remnick's jurisdiction is turned upside down when a prison transport plane crashes in the remote wilderness, setting free dozens of violent inmates. The Last Frontier features Bokenkamp's signature themes, including criminal masterminds, government conspiracies, and complex federal officers. Bokenkamp wrote the show alongside Richard D'Ovidio . With new episodes of staple hits like Slow Horses and The Morning Show rolling out week after week, one would think there would be an all-out war for the top spot on the streamer’s global Top 10. Alas, there is but one title that has sat at the top of the chart since its grand debut aired earlier this month. That would be the Jason Clarke -led action-centered crime thriller, The Last Frontier . In the days since the network’s original series burst onto screens on October 10, audiences around the world have faithfully tuned in to watch the pulse-pounding action and high-stakes drama play out, helping it carve out the number one spot and not let go. Although no Season 2 renewal has been announced at this time, it seems more than likely that the platform will want to push through with more where that came from, considering the show’s global takeover. For those unfamiliar, The Last Frontier channels the things viewers love about shows like Yellowstone and Jack Ryan, then flips them on their head before dropping the main characters into the Alaskan wilderness. Starring Clarke as a US Marshal named Frank Remnick, the story follows a flight filled with some of the country’s most dangerous prisoners after it crashes just outside of Fairbanks, Alaska. With high-risk fugitives now on the loose, Frank has his hands full protecting his beloved town and those closest to him. Meanwhile, the CIA soon gets involved when they discover that one of the runaway convicts is a man they’ve been trying to detain for quite some time. Meet the Team Behind ‘The Last Frontier’ The parallels between The Last Frontier and other hit shows of today or yesteryear aren’t completely hard to understand when you learn that the man behind the series is none other than Jon Bokenkamp . Although he’s been involved in a multitude of other successful small-screen productions, Bokenkamp is best known as the creator behind the 10-season-running James Spader -led crime thriller, The Blacklist . Meanwhile, many of the gorgeous shots that have sucked audiences into The Last Frontier were all under the vision of its frequent director, Sam Hargrave , who fans will know from Netflix’s Extraction film franchise. In addition to Clarke’s leading role as the rough and tough US Marshal, The Last Frontier also features dynamite performances from an impressive ensemble that features the talents of Dallas Goldtooth ( Fallout ), Dominic Cooper ( Mamma Mia ), Simone Kessell ( Yellowjackets ), Haley Bennett ( The Girl on the Train ), Alfre Woodard ( Star Trek: First Contact ) and Tait Blum ( For All Mankind ). Continue Cancel Entertainment 14 Heartwarming Thanksgiving Movies and Specials Get into the holiday spirit with these tasty films and shows By Nicholas DeRenzo, Updated November 21, 2025 AARP Comments En español Published November 18, 2020 / Updated November 21, 2025 A scene from "A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving." AF archive/Alamy Stock Photo Facebook Twitter LinkedIn As families reunite around the table, Thanksgiving is perfect fodder for cinematic drama, both high-stakes (shocking secrets revealed!) and low (someone burned the turkey!). From Pieces of April to Addams Family Values, these are our picks for a 14-course menu of Turkey Day–themed entertainment. Since you won’t want to watch on an empty stomach, we’ve paired each with a dish that will get you in the holiday spirit. Members only Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987) The plot: In John Hughes’ odd-couple classic, uptight marketing executive Neal Page ( Steve Martin , 80) tries desperately to get home to his family for Thanksgiving after a business trip. Along the way, he keeps coming into contact with an annoying but lovable fellow traveler, shower curtain ring salesman Del Griffith (John Candy). A series of mishaps — including a blizzard and a burglar — leave them bonding and bickering, crisscrossing the Midwest on various modes of transportation. The dish: The tiny airplane bottles of international liquor they share in the motel. Watch it: Planes, Trains and Automobiles Pieces of April (2003) The plot: Get the tissues ready. In this heartfelt dramedy, April (Katie Holmes) cooks Thanksgiving dinner in her Lower East Side apartment in an attempt to reconcile with her estranged parents, Jim (Oliver Platt, 65) and Joy (Patricia Clarkson, 65), who is dying of breast cancer. Clarkson was nominated for an Oscar for the role. When her oven breaks, April turns to the neighbors in her building to help her get the meal on the table in time. The dish(es): Sweet potato soup with buttered pecans, herbed oyster stuffing, giblet gravy, lemon-rosemary green beans, sautéed red Swiss chard with garlic, hickory nut ice cream and maple pumpkin pie (her neighbors’ gourmet menu, which puts April’s canned cranberry sauce to shame). Watch it: Pieces of April What's Cooking? (2000) The plot: This L.A.-set dramedy features a sprawling ensemble — including Alfre Woodard, 73; Julianna Margulies, 59; Joan Chen, 64; and Kyra Sedgwick , 60 — and follows four different families (Vietnamese, Jewish, Black and Latino) as they celebrate Thanksgiving in their own unique ways. The menus — which include fresh tortillas, macaroni and cheese, and marshmallow-topped sweet potatoes — may all be different, but you’ll be happy to know that generational gaps and political squabbles cross all cultural divides. The dish: The chile-paste-rubbed turkey that causes the Vietnamese daughter to ask, “Why do you want to make the turkey taste like everything else we eat?” Watch it: What’s Cooking? Addams Family Values (1993) The plot: Leave it to the creepy, kooky crew to poke a hole in a great American tradition. In this cult classic sequel, Wednesday (Christina Ricci) and Pugsley (Jimmy Workman) are sent off to a summer camp, where the counselors, Gary (Peter MacNicol, 71) and Becky (Christine Baranski, 73), try to break the kids of their macabre habits. They cast the siblings in a Thanksgiving pageant — Wednesday as an apocryphal Pocahontas, Pugsley as a turkey — but things take a turn when Wednesday delivers a blistering monologue about Native American history, stages a coup, burns down the set and escapes in the camp van. The dish: The apple Wednesday shoves in the bully’s mouth before attempting to burn her at the stake. Watch it: Addams Family Values ​Friendsgiving (2020) The plot: Best friends Molly (Malin Åkerman) and Abby (Kat Dennings) are all set to spend a low-key Thanksgiving together, until the invite list begins to spiral out of control. Soon, the table is filled with Molly’s Swedish mother ( Jane Seymour , 73), new and ex-lovers, mutual friends (Aisha Tyler, 545 and Deon Cole, 53), children, potential suitors and a “shawoman” (Chelsea Peretti). As the wackiness begins to reach a boiling point, magic mushrooms make an appearance, leading to the arrival of three imaginary “fairy gay mothers” (played by Wanda Sykes , 61; Margaret Cho, 56; and Fortune Feimster). The dish: ’Shrooms (but maybe opt for stuffed or sautéed instead of psychedelic). Watch it: Friendsgiving AARP NEWSLETTERS %{ newsLetterPromoText }% %{ description }% Subscribe See All Newsletters Privacy Hub ARTICLE CONTINUES AFTER ADVERTISEMENT Tower Heist (2011) The plot: When he loses his pension in a Ponzi scheme masterminded by Wall Street businessman Arthur Shaw ( Alan Alda , 89), luxury apartment building manager Josh Kovaks (Ben Stiller, 59) hatches a plan to break into Shaw’s penthouse and steal back the money. He enlists his coworkers — a petty criminal ( Eddie Murphy , 64) and a bankrupt investor (Matthew Broderick, 63) — to pull off the heist of the century during the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. The dish: Revenge — best served cold. Watch it: Tower Heist Members only Home for the Holidays (1995) The plot: Jodie Foster , 63, directs this sweet comedy that proves that you can go home again — though if you do, you might wind up watching your dad spray your brother and brother-in-law with a hose as they fight on the front lawn. When she finds out that her daughter (Claire Danes) has decided to skip Thanksgiving, single mom Claudia (Holly Hunter, 67) flies back to Baltimore to spend the holiday with her parents, played by Anne Bancroft and Charles Durning. When friends, in-laws and siblings arrive (including Robert Downey Jr., 60, as her younger brother Tommy), secrets are revealed, punches are thrown, and the turkey is dropped in someone’s lap. The dish: Sweet potatoes — dotty Aunt Glady (played by Charlie Chaplin’s daughter, Geraldine Chaplin, 81) will eat only the ones she made herself. Watch it: Home for the Holidays Jim Henson’s Turkey Hollow (2015) The plot: Following Yuletide classics such as The Muppet Christmas Carol and Emmet Otter’s Jug-Band Christmas , the Jim Henson Company set its sights on a new holiday in this family-friendly Lifetime movie, with a story conceived by Henson back in 1968. When a divorced dad (Jay Harrington, 54) takes his family to the town of Turkey Hollow for an unplugged Thanksgiving with his eccentric Aunt Cly (Mary Steenburgen, 72), the kids set out into the woods and meet a musical quartet of furry puppet monsters called Squonk, Zorp, Burble and Thrinng. Rapper Ludacris narrates this quirky tale you’ll want to share with your grandkids. The dish: Rock candy, as a nod to the rocks the monsters like to eat. Watch it: Jim Henson’s Turkey Hollow ​ A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving (1973) The plot: This Emmy-winning TV special is as comforting as buttery mashed potatoes, with memorable moments that include Linus’ prayer about the first Thanksgiving, Lucy pulling the football out from under Charlie Brown for the umpteenth time, and Woodstock and Snoopy splitting the wishbone. And even the Peanuts gang isn’t safe from a little dinner table bickering: Peppermint Patty gets annoyed by Charlie Brown’s rather unconventional menu ... The dish: C.B.’s DIY feast (including buttered toast, pretzels, popcorn, jelly beans and an ice cream sundae). Watch it: A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving Garfield’s Thanksgiving (1989) The plot: More of an amuse-bouche than a full meal, this 24-minute holiday special sees everyone’s favorite orange cat receive some devastating news from the vet over the Thanksgiving holiday: He’s overweight and must go on a strict diet — including a measly half a leaf of lettuce for lunch. Garfield’s owner, Jon Arbuckle, has a crush on the doc and invites her over for Thanksgiving, but he’s inept at cooking, resulting in an unthawed turkey and an otherwise disastrous dinner. Showing up at the last minute to save the day is Grandma, who chainsaws the frozen turkey and turns it into croquettes as Jon distracts the vet with boring tales of the first Thanksgiving. The dish: A sensible salad, in honor of Garfield’s diet fare. When they can’t afford a turkey for Thanksgiving, the oldest daughter (played by Emmy-winning Orphan Black star Tatiana Maslany) contacts her rich, estranged grandmother (Jacqueline Bisset, 81) to ask for help, and her arrival stirs up drama and family secrets. If you like Little Women , you’ll find something to love here. The dish: Puddings, which get shouted out by the children many times in both the film and the story on which it’s based. Reggie (Owen Wilson, 57), a domesticated turkey who is pardoned by the president, teams up with wild turkeys Jake (Woody Harrelson, 64) and Jenny (Amy Poehler, 54) to time travel back to the Plymouth Colony in 1621 to keep their kind off the first Thanksgiving menu. During a particularly awkward holiday dinner, his nephew Randy (Bradley Whitford, 66) reveals the shocking way Frank lost his eyesight — but we won’t spoil it for you. The dish: “John” Daniels whiskey; as Frank explains it, “He may be Jack to you, son, but when you’ve known him as long as I have …” Watch it: Scent of a Woman Paul Blart: Mall Cop (2009) The plot: Slate writer Karen Han declared this slapstick-heavy Kevin James, 60, action vehicle an official Thanksgiving movie, dubbing it a “suburban spin on Die Hard .” It’s Black Friday, and the mild-mannered, Segway-riding security guard must take on a gang of burglars who disguise themselves as Santa’s Village employees and plan to rob $30 million from the New Jersey mall where he works. Critics turned the film into a punchline, but it ended up grossing $183.3 million worldwide and even spawned a sequel. The dish: A leftover turkey sandwich filled with mashed potatoes and stuffing, the ultimate way to carbo-load before a Black Friday shopathon — or a Black Friday crime-fighting mission. By Karen Butler 1 of 4 | Haley Bennett and Dominic Cooper star in "The Last Frontier." New episodes stream on Fridays. Photo courtesy of Apple TV. NEW YORK, Oct. 31 (UPI) -- Preacher, Captain America and Mamma Mia! alum Dominic Cooper says his new TV series, The Last Frontier , is compelling entertainment that also explores important themes like truth and morality. "It was a nonstop page turner," Cooper, 47, told UPI in a recent Zoom interview. "Jon Bokenkamp, our show-runner, refers to it as a cheeseburger, which I didn't understand at first. But I think what he means is there's something for everyone and it felt like, and he's described it, a 1990s[-style] blockbuster action piece, but, at the same time, it's complex," Cooper said. "People are desperately needing to follow a complex story-line about issues that are important and reveal truths and lies about the society in which we live." Airing Fridays on Apple TV, the series casts Jason Clarke as Frank, a U.S. Marshal whose quiet life in Alaska is upended when a plane filled with dangerous criminals -- including Cooper's former CIA asset Havlock -- crashes into the snowy mountains under his jurisdiction. Haley Bennett plays Sidney, a CIA agent sent to re-capture Havlock, her husband, while Simone Kessell plays Sarah, a nurse and Frank's wife. The cast also includes Alfre Woodard and Dallas Goldtooth. Magnificent Seven and Hillbilly Elegy actress Bennett, 37, called the show an "epic" story that also depicts intimate interpersonal relationships. "What drew me in about the project was the humanity and the survival and truth and how people hold on to their values when everything is falling apart and what the truth is really changes and transforms over the 10 episodes," she said. "What I love about The Last Frontier is that it feels familiar in all of the best ways and it kind of turns the genre on its head. It's familiar, but it's unexpected and fresh." Cooper added: "Sometimes when you do the complex pieces with great dialogue and really challenging roles with other actors, you go, 'Oh, I really miss doing action.' And then sometimes when you're doing action, you go, 'I just need something more complex.' "This had everything, so I couldn't complain," Cooper laughed. "There's also sex. There's relationships within this nightmare world, which a lot of people have to live in, survival and dealing with the integrity of a country, the diplomacy of a country. At the same time, they're real people. They have to live normal lives, as well. They exist, these people, and I don't know how they do it." Bennett noted that there are big differences between the Alaskans, the plane crash survivors who terrorize them and the shadowy government agents who seem to know more about the whole situation than they are letting on. "There's such a contrast between the community in which Frank is living in, where everybody takes care of each other, and then the world in which they live in, where it's every man for himself," she said. "On a deeper level, beyond the action, what this is a commentary of is, what we are all doing here, what we're all doing and how we get ourselves into morally ambiguous situations." "This is what I've struggled with daily," Cooper agreed. "It's every man for himself now and morals are at an all-time low. People don't know what their moral compass is. We allow politicians to lie now. You can lie. It's official. You're allowed to talk absolute garbage straight-up," he added. "There's no such thing as facts any more." Bennett said she hopes these themes resonate with audiences. " Last Frontier isn't about survival in the wild. It's about emotional survival and what it costs to hold on to your truth," she added. Young actor Tait Blum chatted about starring in the series “The Last Frontier” on Apple TV. Blum stars alongside Jason Clarke, Dominic Cooper, Haley Bennett, Simone Kessell, and Alfre Woodard. Margaret Mead once said: “Never doubt that a small group of thoughtful, committed citizens can change the world; indeed, it’s the only thing that ever has.” This quote applies to Tait Blum, who is a revelation in “The Last Frontier.” Experience making ‘The Last Frontier’ “The Last Frontier” follows Frank Remnick (Jason Clarke), the lone U.S. marshal in charge of the quiet, rugged barrens of Alaska. Remnick’s jurisdiction is turned upside down when a prison transport plane crashes in the remote wilderness, setting free dozens of violent inmates. Tasked with protecting the town he’s vowed to keep safe, he begins to suspect the crash wasn’t an accident, but the first step of a well-crafted plan with far-reaching and devastating implications. On his experience making “The Last Frontier,” he remarked, “It has been amazing! It has been quite a wild ride like the show.” Playing Luke, the son of Jason Clarke’s character On playing Luke, the son of Jason Clarke’s character, he said, “Jason is amazing! He has been doing this for so many years, and he is such a veteran.” “I really loved picking his brain and being on set with him,” he admitted. “Jason is absolutely incredible! I think we look quite a bit alike too, so that’s nice. Our resemblance is almost uncanny.” Lessons learned from this screenplay On the lessons learned from this screenplay, Blum reflected, “It taught me that Luke is such a very brave character, and he is someone who values family so much. Luke is also a loyal character. I realize that through Luke especially that I understand a lot of things about myself.” “I’m very loyal and I would perhaps have reacted the same way and he did because I care about my family so deeply,” Blum noted. “This show brought me together with my family, and I feel that it’s a lesson in loyalty,” he acknowledged. The digital age On being a part of the digital age, Blum said, “I think it’s interesting! I guess I am one of the last generations in the fully digital age.” “It can be a bit overwhelming at times; I have to get away, but I think it’s quite cool,” he added. Advice for young and emerging actors For young and aspiring actors, Blum said, “Rejection is not a bad thing. The more rejections you can take, the better you can handle that, and the better you’re going to be in the long run.” “Grit is so important,” he underscored. “So, just keep pushing forward and continue to do the work; that’s so valuable.” Future plans Regarding his future plans, he shared, “I love making films and doing television so much, and I am just going to keep going whatever comes my way.” “I’ll do whatever project I wind up loving in the same way that I loved this show. I think I’m going to see where the wind takes me, and I will continue to look for character-driven projects like this one,” he explained. Stage of his life On the title of the current chapter of his life, Blum revealed, “A New Beginning.” Superpower of choice Blum’s superpower of choice would be “flight.” “It would be so cool to fly,” he admitted. “I would be able to take off and go wherever I want without having to pay for a ticket.” Success On his definition of the word success, he expressed, “Being able to look back in 40 years and say that ‘I’ve told the stories that I want to tell,’ and that my family is completely taken care of. Also, the peace of mind that comes with that.” Message to his fans For his fans and supporters, Blum said, “First and foremost, I want to say that I love them! My fans are very loyal. I’m super excited to bring them more things to look forward to and to watch.” Closing thoughts on ‘The Last Frontier’ “I just want the fans to have a really good time,” he exclaimed about “The Last Frontier.” “I think that ‘The Last Frontier’ is such an entertaining and explosive show. It’s a fun, vibrant project and I want them to be able to sit back and enjoy it,” Blum concluded. To learn more about actor Tait Blum, follow him on Instagram , and check out his IMDb page .
