Omg, the dramz . Boomer: I stopped watching. Zero respect for our national treasures. SMH*. It’s just a game. They didn’t really murder the Scottish bloke from Casualty . I’m talking about that daft singer asking ‘Who’s Helen Mirren ?’ in an earlier challenge. Cat Burns ? Put some respect on her name. She’s only 25 – and a musical genius. I’m not sure anyone who’s clueless about Helen Mirren and Judi Dench can claim genius status. FR*, I’ve never heard of them either. Helen Mirren? Like, the Helen Mirren?! She’s basically the queen. The only queen I support is Queen B… Not Beyoncé! Helen Mirren played the actual monarch. And won an Oscar for doing so! For Gen Z, Beyoncé rules supreme Nope, never heard of her. Is she on TikTok? Give me strength. Even The Independent ’s been questioning ‘why 25-year-olds have such a blind spot when it comes to Britain’s glitterati’. Jheeez. Why are you getting so pressed about Helen? It’s not just Helen. It’s Gen Z’s ‘inability to love an entertainer for very long without getting bored and ditching them’. In our day, we adored our stars… IK*, IK. That’s why you shared that embarrassing post when the Sex And The City bloke died. *Looks confused* You know… When Carrie says to Big: ‘Your girl is lovely, Hubbell.’ Do you mean Robert Redford? That’s the one! I remember cos his name sounds like a law firm. He wasn’t in Sex And The City , he was a Hollywood icon! No way. Haven’t you seen the TikTok clip from after he died in September? A compilation of his iconic scenes from The Way We Were , I hope… No, it said: ‘All these news stories mean I finally know why Carrie called him Hubbell.’ Blasphemy – the man co-founded Sundance! The fake-tan brand? The Festival ! I’m with The Washington Post : Gen Z are the first generation to have no ‘working knowledge of pop culture that came before them’. Hail Helen, the Boomer queen Well, at least I recognise people who are actually famous now . I have a great knowledge of modern celebrities, I’ll have you know. Oh yeah? Who’s Emma Chamberlain? She’ll be some long-lost descendant of Neville who’s now foraying into modelling, surely? Be serious. She’s a 24-year-old YouTuber who gets four million views per video and is so big, she hosts the Met Gala’s red-carpet coverage. That was a trick question! Give me another… Fine, who hosts Chicken Shop Date ? I don’t know… the CEO of Nando’s? Amelia Dimoldenberg! She was literally in Vogue ! She’s only 31 and she’s basically become the most famous person in the UK. By eating peri-peri chicken wings on YouTube? By hosting hilarious interviews in London chicken shops. I’m not au fait with all those influencer types. I prefer my celebrities to have actual talent. Actual talent? Please. In one TikTok with well over a million views, someone’s Boomer mum refers to nine-time Grammy winner Billie Eilish as ‘Billie Eyelashes’. That’s just a slip of the tongue. In another clip with nearly a million views, someone’s mum calls Timothée Chalamet ‘Timothée Charlamaze’. To be fair to her, it’s not the easiest name to pronounce. The best bit? It wasn’t even ‘Timothée Charlamaze’ in the picture. It was Jeremy Allen White. That’s understandable. They’ve both got that moody and malnourished look. It’s called aesthetic. It’s called anaemia. Come on, there must be some celebrity we both know? Hmmmm. Joan Collins? No clue. What about Lil Nas X? Sounds like a sports car. Maybe Kylie? Yes! The absolute kween and icon! Something we agree on. She and Jason are what you lot would call #couplegoals. Jason? You mean Timothée? I think I know their names. I had a poster of them together on my bedroom wall. You had a poster of Kylie Jenner? No! Minogue. Wait, there are two Kylies? There’s only one that matters. The youngest of the Kardashians? I’m sticking to the 1980s pop icon. Cos you can’t Keep Up with the Kulture ? BBC's The Repair Shop has just announced its exciting hour-long Christmas special, which will welcome some special celebrity guests into its Repair Shop barn, including a certain Hollywood legend. The wonderful The Thursday Murder Club actress Dame Helen Mirren will appear on the show this December and will be looking to expert Becky Houghton for help. What everyone's reading The star will is bringing along a beloved cello, which dates back to the Second World War. BBC/Ricochet It belongs to Denville Hall, which is a care home that looks after people who have worked in the entertainment industry. The actress has always been a loyal supporter of the care home in Northwood in London. The story behind the cello was that it was left to Denville Hall by the theatre director Martin Landau. Originally from Germany, Martin fled the country on the Kinder transport, but unfortunately his cello was broken by the Nazis before he was able to get on the train. The cello hasn't been played in over 80 years, and the care home would love to have it restored so that it can be used alongside the piano they have, to perform Christmas songs, uniting their elderly residents. Excited to feature in the Christmas special, Dame Helen Mirren said: "Denville Hall is a very special place and we’ve long talked about repairing Martin’s cello. As you can imagine to be able to restore the voice of his prized possession and hear it play once more’ will be the greatest Christmas gift for the community at Denville Hall." Dame Helen Mirren isn't the only star to appear in the upcoming Christmas special, Gavin and Stacey's actor Rob Brydon will be entering the barn too. He will appear alongside author Julia Donaldson whose BBC Christmas animated adventure, The Scarecrows' Wedding will appear on our TV screens this festive season. BBC/Ricochet Rob has voiced a character in every one of Julia's animated adaptations and together he and Julia will be seeking a repair on a toy farmhouse that was given to Julia by her granny on the show. The farm was a much-loved toy that was played with by Julia and her sister, and will in turn be gifted to Chestnut Tree House, which is a children’s hospice Julia has a longstanding relationship with and where she has performed many of her stories. The Repair Shop team will also be repairing a much loved life size, mechanical Rudolph, belonging to Leicestershire Fire service, which has brought decades of festive cheer but is currently in a sorry state. As well as Rudolph, the experts will restore a battered and broken sledge that has seen 80 years of service for a family from Northern Ireland, and a dilapidated carol book that has played a central role in a little known but much celebrated local tradition in Sheffield. While we don't have an exact date for the upcoming Christmas special, we will be sure to update you when we do. We can't wait to watch it! The second season of the drama series, based on Laura Dave’s forthcoming sequel novel The First Time I Saw Him , will premiere Friday, February 20, 2026. There will be eight episodes. Related Stories News Everything We Know About ‘The Last Thing He Told Me’ Season 2 Casting ‘The Last Thing He Told Me’ Casts Judy Greer For Season 2 Season 2 will pick up as Owen Michaels (Nikolaj Coster-Waldau) shows up after five years on the run, initiating a race for Hannah Hall (Jennifer Garner) and her stepdaughter Bailey (Angourie Rice) to reunite their family “before the past catches up to them,” as the logline teases. The First Time I Saw Him will publish January 6, 2026, providing a hint at what’s to come for Hannah, Owen, Bailey and more ahead of the Season 2 premiere. Season 1 — which debuted in April 2023 — ended with Owen silently and subtly signaling to Hannah that he was still around by walking through her exhibition heavily disguised. Hannah had made a deal with Bailey’s grandfather Nicholas Bell (played by David Morse) that no harm would come to any of the three of them if Owen agreed to stay far away from Bailey. This is where Dave’s first novel, The Last Thing He Told Me , ended as well. Newcomers in addition to Judy Greer, whose casting Deadline first announced , and Wilson include Michael Galante, John Noble, and Luke Kirby. Missing from the returners is Aisha Tyler, who played Hannah’s best friend Jules Nichols. Season 2 is executive produced by co-showrunners Josh Singer and Aaron Zelman alongside Hello Sunshine’s Reese Witherspoon and Lauren Neustadter. Star Garner also executive produces. Zelman joins Season 2 as co-showrunner. The Last Thing He Told Me is produced by 20th Television and Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine, a part of Candle Media. Created and adapted by Laura Dave, alongside Academy Award-winning co-creator Josh Singer, The Last Thing He Told Me was the first collaboration between the married Dave and Singer, who both serve as executive producers. Aaron Zelman, Daisy von Scherler Mayer and Merri D. Howard also serve as executive producers. A second season of the buzzy Jennifer Garner -led series has filmed and will debut in early 2026, almost three years after Season 1 made its debut. Season 2 is based on Laura Dave 's forthcoming novel The First Time I Saw Him , a sequel to her 2021 book The Last Thing He Told Me , which served as the basis for the television project. The original season marked the first collaboration between Dave and Josh Singer , the married couple who serve as executive producers alongside Garner and Hello Sunshine's Reese Witherspoon and Lauren Neustadter . For Season 2, Aaron Zelman joins as co-showrunner and executive producer with Singer. Daisy von Scherler Mayer and Merri D. Howard are additional executive producers. The last time we checked in on Hannah Hall (Garner), she was working at her art gallery when a heavily bearded man appeared, whom she immediately recognized as her missing husband, Owen ( Nikolaj Coster-Waldau ). He briefly touched her hand and whispered, "The could-have-been boys still love you," a callback to an earlier conversation about her exes. When Season 2 picks up, Hannah and her stepdaughter Bailey ( Angourie Rice ) find themselves in a terrifying race to figure out how to reunite their family before the past catches up to them. Who's in the cast? Garner, Coster-Waldau, and Rice are all back from Season 1, reprising their roles as three members of a dysfunctional family, as Hannah and Bailey are still searching for the missing Owen. Also returning is David Morse as Nicholas Bell, Owen's former father-in-law and Bailey's grandfather who has ties to the mafia. It's not yet known whether Victor Garber , Garner's Alias costar who popped up in Season 1 as Prof. Tobias Cookman, will return for the sequel. New additions to the cast for Season 2 include Rita Wilson , Judy Greer , Augusto Aguilera , Josh Hamilton , Nick Hargrove , Michael Galante , John Noble , Michael Hyatt , and Luke Kirby . What is the premiere date? Mark your calendar for Feb. 20, 2026, as that's when Season 2 will debut on Apple TV. That is almost three years after Season 1 launched on April 14, 2023. How many episodes? While the first season consisted of seven episodes, the upcoming season is slightly longer at eight episodes. Think of how much additional drama the writers can pack into that extra hour! First-look photos On Nov. 5, Apple TV released the first set of photos for Season 2 of The Last Thing He Told Me . The high-res images showcase Garner, Coster-Waldau, Rice, Wilson, and Greer. Eagle-eyed fans will notice the Eiffel Tower in the background of one of the pics, suggesting Garner's character will travel to Paris at some point. A video trailer will be unveiled at a later date. Apple TV 's hit thriller The Last Thing He Told Me is returning for a second season, and judging by the newly released first-look pictures, it's shaping up to be the perfect new year binge. Based on The First Time I Saw Him – Laura Dave's sequel to her bestselling 2021 novel – the series will follow Hannah (Jennifer Garner) as she faces the shocking return of her missing husband five years after his mysterious disappearance. Jennifer Garner, who also serves as executive producer, stars alongside returning cast members Angourie Rice, David Morse and Nikolaj Coster-Waldau . © Courtesy of Apple You know you're in safe hands when a show comes from Reese Witherspoon's production company Hello Sunshine, and The Last Thing He Told Me is no exception. Ben Affleck is caught in the crossfire amid Jennifer Lopez and Jennifer Garner’s holiday disagreements Shivani Negi | Nov 25, 2025, 08:56 IST ( Image credit : X/@PopTingz | Ben Affleck caught between JLo and Jennifer Garner’s holiday feud ) Ben Affleck is reportedly stuck between Jennifer Lopez and Jennifer Garner as the two differ on how his kids should spend the holidays, with one favouring a getaway and the other wanting to stay in LA. Ben Affleck just can’t seem to catch a break when it comes to his Jennifer drama. The 53-year-old actor is reportedly caught in a tense back-and-forth as Jennifer Garner and Jennifer Lopez struggle to agree on holiday plans, creating friction as they try to navigate their complicated blended family arrangement. Ben Affleck's exes feuding over holiday arrangements According to a National Enquirer report, JLo, 56, and Garner, 53, each have their own ideas about how the holiday schedule should work with Affleck’s three children. Their conflicting preferences have allegedly left Affleck stuck in the middle, trying to keep everyone calm while managing growing tension. ( Image credit : X/@21metgala | Jennifer Lopez and Jennifer Garner are clashing over holiday plans, leaving Ben Affleck caught in the middle. ) The tabloid claims the two women can’t agree on where Affleck and the children should spend the festive season, leading to fresh strain in an already delicate dynamic. Lopez and Garner split over holiday plans According to the report, Lopez, 56, has suggested taking Affleck and his children Violet, 20, Fin, 16, and Samuel, 13, whom he shares with Garner, on a tropical getaway for the holidays. The unnamed sources claim she believes a trip would give the family quality time together and offer the kids a break from the constant public attention surrounding their parents. Garner, 53, on the other hand, is said to prefer keeping the holidays close to home in Los Angeles. The outlet’s insiders describe her as hesitant about disrupting the children’s routine, noting that she and Affleck have long focused on providing stability and consistency since their 2018 divorce. ( Image credit : X/@ThePopTingz | Jennifer Lopez and Ben Affleck with his daughter Violet ) Affleck is reportedly juggling pressure from both households, though these claims have not been verified by any of the family members. Notably, despite Affleck and JLo's 2024 divorce, the Jenny on the Block hitmaker is said to share a close-knit bond with his children and is often seen spending time with them on casual outings. Affleck is also close to JLo's twins, whom she shares with her ex-husband Marc Anthony. Jennifer Lopez and Ben Affleck's roller-coaster romance: From 2000s love to a 2024 split Ben Affleck and Jennifer Lopez first fell in love in the early 2000s after meeting on the set of their film Gigli . Famously dubbed “Bennifer”, they got engaged in 2002 and planned to marry in 2003, but called it off just days before the wedding due to intense media scrutiny. ( Image credit : X/@PopFaction | Ben Affleck and Jennifer Lopez’s on-again romance ends in a 2025 divorce after two decades of highs and reconciliations. ) Nearly two decades later, the pair rekindled their relationship in 2021, re-engaged, and finally tied the knot in a quick Las Vegas ceremony in July 2022 (followed by a larger celebration in Georgia). Yet by April 2024, things had already soured; Lopez later filed for divorce in August, citing “irreconcilable differences”. The divorce was finalised in January 2025. About Jennifer Garner and Ben Affleck's relationship The Gone Girl actor and 13 Going on 30 fame began their relationship in 2004 after meeting on the sets of Pearl Harbour and Daredevil . They were engaged in April 2005 and married in June 2005 in a private ceremony in Turks and Caicos. They had three children together before announcing their separation in 2015. ( Image credit : X/@PopBase | Ben Affleck and Jennifer Garner keep co-parenting strong after 2015 split ) Despite the split, they continued to co-parent their children amicably, often living together for a time and supporting each other. Their divorce was officially filed in 2017 and finalised in October 2018, with joint legal and physical custody arrangements for their kids. They have maintained a cooperative co-parenting relationship focused on their children's well-being despite the divorce. She models empathy, navigates co-parenting with honesty, and sets firm boundaries, like delaying social media access. Garner emphasizes one-on-one time and adapting her parenting approach to each child's unique needs, fostering resilience and independence. Jennifer Garner may be one of Hollywood’s most beloved actresses, but at home, she’s simply Mom, dedicated to raising Violet, Seraphina, and Samuel with kindness, gratitude and a strong sense of purpose. Amid a busy career, charity work and a life constantly under public scrutiny, Garner has carved out a clear parenting philosophy. Her approach blends compassion, boundaries, individuality and honest communication. Over the years, she has opened up through interviews and podcasts about the values she wants her kids to grow up with and the everyday choices she makes to guide them. The power of kindness For Jennifer Garner, parenting begins with modeling kindness not lecturing about it. In a 2022 interview with Parents, she said the most effective way to raise kind children is to demonstrate it in simple, visible ways. “I think the most powerful thing to do is to live it,” she shared. Garner believes children learn empathy when they watch you extend it to neighbors, friends, or strangers. Whether that means dropping off a meal to someone in need or involving them in meaningful community work, she wants her kids to see kindness as a normal part of daily life. Through action, not words, she teaches them that giving back is part of being a good human. Mindful parenting: Cultivating emotional intelligence in kids The importance of respectful co-parenting Raising kids in a blended, high-profile family is not easy, but Garner has long prioritized stability and respect. After her divorce from Ben Affleck in 2018, she made it a point to keep communication honest and age-appropriate. Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter, she explained how she guided her children through tabloid stories and public scrutiny. “If you see an image on the front of a magazine, I’ll look at it with you and we’ll process all the scary feelings that come up together,” she told them. Now that her kids are older and have more access to outside information, she knows she cannot control everything yet the foundation she built ensures they feel safe talking about anything. For Garner, respectful co-parenting isn’t about being perfect; it’s about staying united where it matters most. Parenting teens in the age of social media Jennifer Garner openly admits she doesn’t have all the answers, especially when it comes to today’s digital pressures. But she is firm on one boundary: her kids don’t have social media. On The Today Show, she revealed her rule, one backed by research rather than trend. “Show me the articles that prove social media is good for teenagers, and then we’ll have the conversation,” she told her kids. Her oldest, Violet, has actually expressed gratitude for this protective stance. Still, Garner acknowledges it’s a long journey with two younger children approaching the same age. Her approach reflects thoughtful parenting: not banning out of fear, but setting boundaries with evidence, openness, and a willingness to revisit the conversation. The importance of alone time with each kid As children grow, their emotional worlds become more complex and more guarded. Garner believes one-on-one time is essential to keeping those doors open. She told Today Parents that she considers bedtime “sacred,” carving out individual moments with each child whenever possible. These quiet windows often lead to unexpected conversations or confessions that reveal what her kids are truly feeling. By being present and attentive, she ensures each child feels seen and valued. This practice, she says, strengthens trust and keeps communication flowing even in the busy teenage years. Learning to parent each kid differently and growing as a mom Parenting, for Jennifer Garner, is an ongoing process of trial, learning, and evolution. With three kids, she quickly realised that what worked for her firstborn didn’t always apply to the second or third. On the Mom Brain podcast, she reflected on how she gradually let go of rigid rules and allowed flexibility to grow with each child. From obsessing over nap schedules with her first to embracing stroller naps with her youngest, she learned to adapt rather than control. Her biggest lesson came with her third child: “Prepare your child for the path, instead of preparing the path for your child.” It’s a mindset that encourages resilience, problem-solving and independence values she hopes her children carry into adulthood. Comments News Hayley Anderson TV Reporter 08:15, 03 Nov 2025 A Steven Spielberg film that's been praised as "one of the best" is almost ready to stream. ‌ The 2002 comedy-drama Catch Me If You Can draws from con artist Frank Abagnale Jr's semi-autobiographical book, exploring how he managed to pull off his sophisticated scams. ‌ Abagnale, brought to life by Hollywood legend Leonardo DiCaprio , manages to masquerade as a pilot, doctor and lawyer whilst cashing fraudulent cheques worth millions before turning 21. ‌ The captivating film reveals not only how the fraudster operated but also how he managed to evade capture from FBI agent Carl Hanratty (portrayed by Tom Hanks ). Now, over two decades since its original cinema release, Catch Me If You Can will be accessible for streaming. View 2 Images Director Steven Spielberg was behind the 2002 film Catch Me If You Can. (Image: GETTY) ‌ The wait is nearly finished as Catch Me If You Can becomes available to watch from Friday, November 7, on Paramount+. To access Paramount+'s library, you'll need to buy a monthly subscription with the basic plan featuring adverts priced at £4.99 per month or £7.99 for the premium plan without ads. Alternatively, the basic package comes at no additional charge for Sky Cinema subscribers. ‌ Beyond being helmed by visionary Steven Spielberg, who created other masterpieces like Jurassic Park, ET and Saving Private Ryan, Catch Me If You Can boasts an exceptional cast. Alongside DiCaprio and Hanks, the early 2000s film stars The Deer Hunter's Christopher Walken, Grey's Anatomy favourite Ellen Pompeo, 13 Going on 30's Jennifer Garner and The Better Sister actor Elizabeth Banks. View 2 Images Tom Hanks stars as FBI Agent Carl Hanratty in the 2002 film Catch Me If You Can. (Image: DREAMWORKS PICTURES) ‌ Catch Me If You Can has been a massive hit with audiences over the years, securing an outstanding 96% rating on the review aggregator site Rotten Tomatoes. "This is one of the best movies I've ever seen. It had everything - great actors, great music by John Williams and amazing direction from Steven Spielberg", a fan praised. Another wrote: "Catch Me If You Can whisked me into a world of slick confidence and irresistible charm from the moment it kicked off." Article continues below Meanwhile, a third commented: "Outstanding, and 100% an entertaining suspense packed thriller. "It is a masterpiece of direction with the unmatchable acting skills of DiCaprio and Tom Hanks." Catch Me If You Can arrives on Friday, November 7, on Paramount+. While there are all sorts of great ideas online, sometimes a great recipe just falls into your lap, like this sweet potato pudding, shared by Jennifer Garner on her Instagram account some years ago. Over the years, Garner has shown all sorts of dishes on her social media, sharing them on her "Pretend Cooking Show," a series of videos where she informally shares a recipe and cooks it to completion. Garner has a soft spot for desserts, with one of the best being her Grandmother's sweet potato pudding, which she shared some years ago on her Instagram. In a video shared on her account, Garner revealed she'd initially shared the recipe with Ina Garten 's Barefoot Contessa show, one of her favorites cooking programs. "Grandma calls for two and a half cups of sugar. That is so much sugar," says Garner in the video as she prepares the recipe while wearing a black top. She's careful in dispensing the ingredients and the sugar, tasting some of the batter with her pinky. Garner then looks at the camera, adding the remaining cup of sugar. © NBC Garner often shares amazing recipes on her social media "Happy Thanksgiving! Pretend Cooking Show was invited to share a family recipe with the one and only Barefoot Contessa —easy as pie — Exie Mae’s Sweet Potato Pudding," she wrote in her post's caption. "Now my darling Ina Garten has been kind enough to share Grandma’s pudding on her special Thanksgiving episode! In case you missed it last night on Food Network— the full episode is on IGTV," she wrote. She then proceeded to list out the recipe, which you can check out below. View post on Instagram Exie Mae Garner’s Sweet Potato Pudding "There are tons of ways to make this less rich—but is this really the week to go crazy?" continued Garner. "Thank you, Ina, for having me. And thank you, Grandma, for a recipe that tastes like you made it and is everything cozy and delicious about Thanksgiving." Ingredients: 4 medium red sweet potatoes 3 cups milk 2 ½ cups sugar 3 tbsp oleo or butter Nutmeg Allspice Cinnamon 3 eggs, beaten 1 bag of miniature marshmallows Directions: Peel and quarter sweet potatoes. Boil until tender and drain, then mash/beat with a beater. Add milk, sugar, butter, and spices to suit taste. Beat 3 eggs and add them in. Tip the pudding into a buttered 9x13 baking dish. Cook at 350 for about an hour, until nearly done. Turn the oven to broil. Spread marshmallows on top and put back in for about 2 minutes until browned. By Andy Swift Nov. 4, 2025 7:00 pm EST Hulu Ryan Murphy's new legal drama "All's Fair," starring Kim Kardashian as a founding partner at an all-female divorce law firm, is finally having its day in court, and the verdict is... pretty rough. For a myriad reasons, TV critics are taking special pleasure in tearing down the new Hulu series, which dropped its first three episodes on Tuesday. You can just picture them at their keyboards, giggling quietly to themselves as they feverishly pound out their scathing take-downs. The Hollywood Reporter called it "unforgivably dull," Variety called it "clumsy" in its storytelling and "condescending" in its supposedly feminist messaging, and The Times went so far as to say that it "may be the worst TV drama ever." For the record, we're not here to refute those reviews. Kardashian's acting, for one thing, has not improved since her disappointing turn in "American Horror Story," and the show gives her too much heavy lifting for someone with her dramatic limitations. We would, however, like to shift the conversation towards one very important name that most of these reviews conveniently gloss over: Sarah. Paulson. Sarah Paulson's Performance Makes All's Fair Worth Watching Hulu Allow us to set the scene: Paulson plays Carrington Lane, a rival divorce attorney who hates the show's core four — Allura Grant (Kardashian), Liberty Ronson (Naomi Watts), Emerald Greene (Niecy Nash-Betts) and Dina Standish (Glenn Close) — with a burning passion, deeply bitter towards them for leaving her behind at a male-dominated firm to start their own 10 years ago. Carrington's motivations are a bit more complicated than that, but her mission is clear: to cut down Allura's team at every turn, be it with an underhanded legal chess move or a psyche-shattering insult, both of which typically involve dropping a c-bomb or two. Speaking of which, that particular word — one you neither want to overuse nor misuse, lest it feel gratuitous — is a bit of a delicate weapon, one Paulson handles like a graceful katana. No matter how many times she says it, it always cuts. But it truly cannot be overstated how much Paulson's phenomenally unhinged performance saves this show. In some ways — the best ways, really — it feels like Murphy has given us Sue Sylvester 2.0, only this time she's traded her tracksuit for a power suit and she's allowed to swear. Who else but a spiritual successor to Sue could stare Close in the face and tell her she looks like George Washington? And Can We Talk About Some Of Those Guest Stars? Hulu There's also some fun to be found in the show's divorce-of-the-week format, for which "All's Fair" has recruited an exciting roster of guest actresses. Come on, Judith Light ("Transparent," "Ugly Betty") as a sassy Manhattan socialite? Elizabeth Berkley ("Saved by the Bell") as a scorned scientist? Jessica Simpson ("Newlyweds: Nick and Jessica") as a plastic surgery victim out for revenge? Every casting feels like a gay fever dream, each one gayer and more feverish than the last. In fact, "gay fever dream" is an accurate description for "All's Fair" as a whole, consistent with most of the shows Murphy has given us throughout his career. It's fun, flashy fluff, and if you're looking to enjoy an hour of television with your brain turned all the way off (which is fine!), it might be worth giving the show a chance before making your own ruling. What say you, people of the online jury? Have you checked out any of "All's Fair," and what do you think? (Do you at least agree about Paulson?) Facebook Instagram Twitter TikTok YouTube Subscribe Search Language English Español Entertainment Kim Kardashian’s ‘All’s Fair’ Receives Harsh Reviews From Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic and More By Elise Nelson November 4, 2025 TOP STORIES Click to share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Click to share on X (Opens in new window) X Kim Kardashian Disney/Ser Baffo Tap Here To Add Us Weekly As A Trusted Source Add as a preferred source on Google Kim Kardashian ’s new legal drama, All’s Fair , has yet to impress the TV critics. The Hulu series debuted its first three episodes on Tuesday, November 4, with a zero percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes ’ Tomatometer, which measures the percentage of professional critics who give a film or TV show a positive review. Meanwhile, on Metacritic , All’s Fair currently has a Metascore of 11 out of 100 — described as being “overwhelmingly disliked” by critics — and a user score of 2.4 out of 10, or “generally unfavorable” among viewers. In a zero-star review from The Guardian , TV critic Lucy Mangan wrote that she “did not know it was still possible to make television this bad.” “I assumed that there was some sort of baseline, some inescapable bedrock knowledge of how to do it that now prevents any entry into the art form from falling below a certain standard. But I was wrong,” Mangan continued. “The new series from Ryan Murphy , All’s Fair — starring Kim Kardashian, Naomi Watts and Niecy Nash as the founders of an all-female law firm delivering divorce-y justice to incredibly rich but slightly unlucky women under the azure skies of California – is terrible. Fascinatingly, incomprehensibly, existentially terrible.” Related: Sarah Paulson Praises Kim Kardashian's Acting in New Show 'All's Fair' Steve Granitz/FilmMagic Kim Kardashian is impressing her new costar, Sarah Paulson. Paulson, 49, stars alongside Kardashian, 44, in All’s Fair, an upcoming legal drama executive produced by Ryan Murphy, and was full of praise for the reality television star turned actress. “It’s wonderful,” Paulson told Variety of working alongside Kardashian at the Los Angeles premiere […] The Times ’ deputy TV editor Ben Dowell also gave the show zero stars, writing that the series “may be the worst TV drama ever” in the review’s headline. “Because All’s Fair (Disney+) is so bad, it’s not even enjoyably so. It thinks it’s a feminist fable about spirited lawyers getting their own back on cruel rich men but is in fact a tacky and revolting monument to the same greed, vanity and avarice it supposedly targets,” he wrote. “All scripted, it feels, by a toddler who couldn’t write ‘bum’ on a wall.” Dowell wrote of Kardashian, 45, “Does Kardashian (who plans to take bar exams, we are told) make a convincing lawyer? No, she does not. She is to acting what Genghis Khan is to a peaceful liberal democracy, though of course the dialogue — a tsunami of clunking cliché that drowns this whole enterprise in the first five minutes — doesn’t help her cause.” Meanwhile, The Hollywood Reporter critic Angie Han described both Kardashian’s acting as lawyer Allura Grant and the writing as “stiff and affectless without a single authentic note.” Kim Kardashian, Naomi Watts Disney/Ser Baffo “Her very presence, which succeeds at generating buzz and not much else, feels fitting for a show that seems to want not to be watched so much as mined for viral bits and pieces,” Han added. All’s Fair follows a team of female divorce attorneys who open their own practice in Los Angeles. In addition to Kardashian, Watts, 57, and Nash, 55, the series stars Teyana Taylor , Glenn Close and Sarah Paulson . “Fierce, brilliant, and emotionally complicated, they navigate high-stakes breakups, scandalous secrets, and shifting allegiances — both in the courtroom and within their own ranks. In a world where money talks and love is a battleground, these women don’t just play the game — they change it,” the synopsis reads. Kardashian previously worked with Murphy, 59, on American Horror Story season 12, receiving mostly positive critical reviews for her performance as publicist Siobhan Corbyn. Thank You! That said, Close added, “She was smart enough to have people around her who she could learn from.” Close stars alongside Kardashian, Sarah Paulson, Naomi Watts, Teyana Taylor, and Niecy Nash-Betts in the Hulu series. Edward Berthelot/WireImage Close explained, “If she was a big ego or what I call a ‘life-is-too-short person,’ I would have been unhappy, but she’s not.” Kardashian seems to have made positive impressions on all of the show’s main cast, as each has complimented the reality TV star as “kind” and “hard-working” after filming together. After recruiting Lady Gaga for Season 5 and Season 6, the popular FX show has added another major pop star to the crew. It has been announced that Ariana Grande has joined the cast of American Horror Story Season 13. She will be joined alongside a host of franchise regulars, including Jessica Lange, Sarah Paulson , Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, Kathy Bates, Emma Roberts, Billie Lourd, Gabourey Sidibe and Leslie Grossman. Ryan Murphy Productions announced the cast of Season 13 on Instagram with a brief teaser, and although it doesn't reveal any plot details, the extensive cast list hints that this may be the most ambitious season yet. The last season, subtitled Delicate , followed Emma Roberts as Anna Victoria Alcott, a rising actress in pursuit of becoming a mother when a sinister force begins to haunt her. Reviews are a bit mixed , highlighting the slow-paced nature of the season and the inclusion of Kim Kardashian in a prominent role. The horror anthology series is not afraid to break formula and focus on unexpected storylines, but some fans suspect that Season 13 might be a follow-up to a previous season. Coven and Apocalypse are some of the most popular guesses, especially since a fan-favorite is finally making her grand return. Jessica Lange Coming Back for 'American Horror Story' Is a Big Deal While fans have long speculated that American Horror Story Season 13 might be the last one, the long-awaited return of franchise icon Jessica Lange may support that theory. The last time she showed up in the anthology series was when she reprised her role as Constance Langdon in Apocalypse , Season 8. Lange plainly dismissed a possible return earlier this year, but that has clearly changed. Getting the crew together for one massive cast seems like the recipe for a final hurrah, even if FX or co-creator Ryan Murphy has not revealed that to be the case. Still, fans will embrace Lange's return with open arms, especially alongside other regulars like Sarah Paulson and Emma Roberts. No matter the case, viewers will be treated to another batch of AHS episodes when the series returns on October 31, 2026 . Adding Ariana Grande will only add to the hype, who is expected to reemerge in the Oscar race when Wicked: For Good hits theaters in November. But the big draw for longtime fans is seeing the old faces together again, which seems to be the driving force behind Season 13. In late 2024, Murphy told Variety that he was formulating the next season alongside Paulson, who was keen on getting the previous cast back together. “I did have a wonderful conversation with Sarah Paulson the other day, and she was like, ‘Okay, I think it’s time we get the band back together, so let’s make some calls here.'" Picture: VALERIE MACON/AFP via Getty Images By Katie Louise Smith AHS season 13 is finally on the way... but it's going to be a VERY long wait for fans. Listen to this article Loading audio... Good news: American Horror Story is finally coming back! Even better news: Jessica Lange and Evan Peters are returning ! And now for the bad news: We're all gonna have to wait an entire year to watch it... In case you hadn't heard, AHS season 13 is finally in the works. Nine returning cast members have been announced so far, including Sarah Paulson , Jessica Lange, Evan Peters , Kathy Bates and Angela Bassett hinting at a potential return to Coven . Ariana Grande has also joined the cast. Right at the end of the cast announcement video shared by Ryan Murphy on Instagram, a specific date pops up. Unfortunately, that date is a verrrry long time away. One year, to be exact. Here's everything we know so far about when American Horror Story season 13 is set to be released. Read more: American Horror Story season 13 cast revealed with Jessica Lange returning When does AHS season 13 come out? Sarah Paulson and Evan Peters are both returning to American Horror Story season 13. Picture: Alamy American Horror Story season 13 release date: When does it come out? For those hoping to watch a brand new season of AHS in 2025, you're sadly not in luck. In fact, you're going to have to wait an entire year before you see Jessica Lange back in action... American Horror Story season 13 will be released at Halloween in 2026. While that may hint at October 31st 2026, the exact date has not yet been confirmed. Previous seasons usually aired on Wednesdays or Thursdays but next year's Halloween lands on a Saturday. We'll update this page as soon as we have confirmation of the exact release date. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ryan Murphy Productions (@ryanmurphyproductions) The one-year wait now means it's the longest AHS fans have gone without a new season. AHS: Delicate dropped in September 2023, and ended after a lengthy delay in April 2024. With the exception of 2020 which had to be postponed because of the pandemic, 2025 was the first ever year that there has been no new season of AHS . For all the latest information about American Horror Story season 13, including the potential theme and full cast list so far, you can catch up and read it all right here . NASA rejects Kim Kardashian's claim moon landing 'didn't happen' NASA has hit back at reality TV star Kim Kardashian's claim that the 1969 Moon landing "didn't happen," a theory consistently debunked over decades. "Yes, we've been to the Moon before... 6 times!" NASA acting administrator Sean Duffy wrote on social media platform X. Kardashian made the comments on the latest episode of her long-running TV series The Kardashians, telling co-star Sarah Paulson she thought the Moon landing "didn't happen". Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin took the first steps on the Moon's surface during the Apollo 11 mission but conspiracy theories about the Moon landing have swirled for nearly 50 years. "I'm sending you a million articles with both Buzz Aldrin and the other one," Kardashian tells co-star Sarah Paulson. Kardashian then reads a quote allegedly from Aldrin, responding to a question about the scariest moment of the expedition. "There was no scary moment because it didn't happen. It could've been scary, but it wasn't because it didn't happen," she said. It remains unclear to which article Kardashian was referring or whether the comments were from Aldrin, wo was alleged to have punched a man in 2022 for harassing him about the Apollo 11 mission being a hoax. Speaking with producers in the episode, Kardashian again claims the space mission was "fake" and cites "a few videos on Buzz Aldrin talking about how it didn't happen." "He says it all the time now in interviews," she said. Duffy tagged Kardashian in his X post and highlighted the Artemis mission, NASA's current moon exploration program. "We won the last space race and we will win this one too," he said before inviting Kardashian to the Kennedy Space Center for the mission's launch. He had a moment of struggle trying to grasp Gen Z slang terms, leading to many hilarious reactions. Glenn Close responds to All’s Fair costars’ Gen Z lingo Ahead of the debut of All’s Fair, the stars, Glenn Close , Kim Kardashian, Naomi Watts, Sarah Paulson, Teyana Taylor, and Niecy Nash, sat down for an interview with PEOPLE . Amidst various interesting topics, the group moved to discuss Teyana Taylor’s Oscar nod. Taylor mentioned she was out of town, but Paulson responded with, “It’s because you were busy getting ready to get nominated for an Oscar.” Oh my god,” Taylor said shyly, but Paulson continued teasing her, switching to Gen Z slang (via Parade ). Paulson asked, “What is it?” before figuring it out. She continued, “Ate! Ate! Ate! Chop! Chop!” with hand signals. She dropped another term, “clock-it.” Throughout this conversation, where the others threw words like “ate” and “clock it,” Glenn Close appeared completely lost. The iconic actress could be seen looking around rather aimlessly, mimicking some hand signs, but evidently lost in a very relatable way. “I have no idea what you’re talking about,” she finally said after the initial moment of buffering. Paulson reassured her, “I know. But I’m gonna tell you later and you’re gonna be very excited about it.” This clip has gone viral since many could relate to Close’s reaction to Gen Z slang. There’s something so nostalgic about shopping in busy malls, hanging up a flip phone, and gathering the family for an unhinged, totally awkward holiday gathering. Enter: The Family Stone , a 2005 holiday masterpiece starring Rachel McAdams, Claire Danes, Sarah Jessica Parker, and the late Diane Keaton — not to mention all the men, including Dermot Mulroney, Luke Wilson, and Craig T. Nelson. This star-packed holiday rom-com has the wit, charm, and cozy antics that only a movie from the early aughts could achieve, and now, it might finally be time to get the fam back together. Keep reading for everything we know about the rumored sequel to this heartwarming holiday classic. THE FAMILY STONE, Rachel McAdams, Diane Keaton, Sarah Jessica Parker, 2005, TM & Copyright (c) 20th Century Fox Film Corp. All rights reserved. ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection If you need a refresher, The Family Stone is about the close-knit Stone family, who gathers together for Christmas to meet son Everrett’s (Mulroney) girlfriend Meredith Morton (Parker). Family matriarch Sybil (Keaton) tells the family during the gathering that she was diagnosed with a terminal illness. Hilariously awkward antics ensue, like they tend to do at family get-togethers, and this film continues to hold up after 20 years. Is it sad to say we almost prefer hanging out with the Stones than at our own extended family get-togethers? It’s no different than enjoying the Griswalds or the McCallisters! Will There Be The Family Stone 2 ? THE FAMILY STONE, Brian White, Savannah Stehlin, Ty Giordano, Sarah Jessica Parker, Dermot Mulroney, Elizabeth Reaser, Diane Keaton, Craig T. Nelson, Rachel McAdams, 2005, TM & Copyright (c) 20th Century Fox Film Corp. All rights reserved. ©20thCentFox/Courtesy Everett Collection Twenty years after The Family Stone came out, writer and director Thomas Bezucha revealed that he is working on a sequel, one that eerily echoes reality as the family matriarch and film’s leading actress has died. “I’ve been haunted by the loss of Sybil for months now while I worked on it, and so this was a blow on a tender bruise already,” Bezucha recently told CNN . “Mentally, I’ve been spending time in that house where I’ve been missing her for a while already.” After Keaton’s death last month, Bezucha was inspired to “honor her even more” and “do a good job by the rest of the cast.” What Actors Have Signed On? The 20 th Century Fox film has a big-name cast, but so far, none of those names have signed on for a sequel. According to Bezucha, he contacted The Family Stone ’s producer when he came up with an idea for a second movie and said he would only do it if the principal cast wanted to. “I’m not interested in the Brady family reunion without the original Jan,” he told CNN, adding that despite the unanimously positive responses from the cast, no one has officially signed, and the sequel hasn’t been greenlit yet. (Hopefully that’ll change soon!) For now, we’ll just have to re-watch the original (again), which is available for streaming now on Hulu and Disney+ . Well, if you’re hoping for some outrageous horror, Raimi promises that you won’t be let down by Send Help . Sam Raimi tells Empire Online in a new interview this week, “[Damian Shannon and Mark Swift] pitched the story, and I laughed and couldn’t believe they were doing this.” “It was really outrageous, even for me, who makes outrageous horror films.” While Raimi does note that Send Help shares some passing similarities to The Evil Dead , he also makes it clear that his new movie will deliver a horror of an entirely different kind. “There is a similarity,” Raimi muses, “but it’s not some outside force they’re dealing with here. What they’re coming to terms with is who they really are. And as the layers start shedding, we see certain conflicts emerge.” Watch the previously released Send Help trailer below. Rachel McAdams and Dylan O’Brien star in Send Help , in theaters January 30, 2026 . The news follows close after the death of screen legend Diane Keaton , who portrayed the Stone family matriarch, Sybil, in the 2005 movie, which was originally produced by the now Disney-owned 20th Century Fox. In an interview with CNN , Bezucha revealed his he's working on a script for The Family Stone 2 to " honor [Keaton] even more ," while also noting that there's more pressure to get the sequel right and " do a good job by the rest of the cast " following the actress' passing this year. However, the director-writer explained that he still needs to deliver the final version of his new script to the studio. Bezucha also told his producer that he would only begin to write a sequel to The Family Stone if the main original cast was interested in returning. After reaching out to the actors, Bezucha received positive responses from all of them. The film's principal actors include Sarah Jessica Parker, Rachel McAdams, Dermot Mulroney, Luke Wilson, Elizabeth Reaser, Craig T. Nelson, Claire Danes, and Tyrone Giordano, which would call for another star-packed outing in the Stone family's story. Meredith (Sarah Jessica Parker) greeting the Stone family (Nelson, Keaton and McAdams) Though The Family Stone 's original cast has expressed their interest in a sequel, none of the actors have officially signed onto the film , nor has The Family Stone 2 been confirmed by any studio. However, cast members like Nelson and Mulroney had noted in recent weeks that there were talks about getting a sequel together. The 2005 movie followed Christmas with the Stone family as all five adult siblings, Everett (Mulroney), Susannah (Reaser), Ben (Wilson), Thad (Giordano), and Amy (McAdams), returned to the home of their parents, Sybil (Keaton) and Kelly (Nelson). However, this Christmas put the family to the test as Everett brought home his new girlfriend, Meredith (Parker), whom he intends to propose to despite clashing with his family members. To feel more at ease, Meredith invites her sister, Julie (Danes), to Christmas at the Stone home, adding another layer to the holiday chaos. The film's success in theaters is more impressive given it was released against major franchise blockbusters The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe (which earned over $745 million) and King Kong (earning a $557 million haul). Although its critical reception remains mixed, with The Family Stone currently holding a 52% score from critics on Rotten Tomatoes, the holiday dramedy's star power (including one of Diane Keaton's most celebrated roles ), distinctive humor, and atmosphere have made it an annual must-watch at Christmas for the past two decades. The Family Stone 's legacy and nostalgia have now cemented it as a holiday classic , which makes it all the more surprising that it's taken 20 years to finally get a sequel in development. Culture Lameah Nayeem Published November 3, 2025 Image: 20th Century Fox/Paramount Pictures TikTok is home to many a bewildering term, particularly when it comes to relationships. From breadcrumbing and phubbing, to the group 7 and 67 memes, there are so many words to get across that it can be hard to keep up. The latest to enter the clock app dictionary? “Crackship.” Confused? We’ve got you covered… What Does Crackship Mean? The term crackship is a fusion of “crack,” a slang term for cocaine, and and “ship,” a fanfiction term, shortened from ‘relationship’, used to express the desire to see two people enter a romantic or sexual entanglement. It is a bewildering coupling rooted in absolutely nothing substantial, so far removed from the realm of possibility you’d have to be off your face to even conceive it. Case in point: Regina George and Rodrick Heffley. Over the past week, edits of this unlikely couple have been spawning across social media, depicting a fiery romance full of sass and, strangely enough, some tenderness. Crack-ships have been around for a while. Some Love Island US fans might remember how Olandria and Nick started out as a throwaway joke on online forums, with viewers gleefully overanalysing every accidental glance and brush of the hand. Against all odds, a series of chaotic events actually brought their relationship into reality, but the Regina x Rodrick fantasies occupy a more fascinating space. @loafofdeath POV: rodrick tries to throw a party without telling regina, but she finds out. || #diaryofawimpykid #edit #meangirls #reginageorge #rodrickheffley ♬ original sound - loaf It all began with fanart by artist @monia_lynn , captioned “I MIGHT be a genius.” The drawing, posted on Instagram and TikTok, snowballed into a full-blown phenomenon. Fans began crafting edits, comparing traits, and spinning elaborate analyses on what made the queen bee of North Shore High such an oddly compelling match with the grungy drummer of homegrown band L ö ded Diper. Edits feature clips spliced from Mean Girls and Diary of a Wimpy Kid, stitched together into faux scenes of banter and flirtatious disdain. The craziest part? Just how well the two actually work together. Regina’s cunning is perfectly parried by Rodrick’s spunk. They share a penchant for mockery and would, without a doubt, trade insults about you behind your back. Of course, this isn’t the first crack-ship to capture the internet’s imagination. In recent years, we’ve seen Tiana from The Princess and the Frog paired with Nanami Kento, the demon-hunting salaryman from Jujutsu Kaisen ; and one of the most enduring examples feature Jack Frost and Elsa, whose MovieMaker union dominated Tumblr throughout the 2010s. @everythinga_ prometo que eu vou parar #reginageorge #rodrickheffley #meangirls #diaryofawimpykid #fyp ♬ som original - 🎐 everythinga_ Where Do They Come From? The philosophy of the crack-ship is simple: it thrives on delusion, wild imagination, and an eye for potential in the most implausible of places. For some, the joy in stumbling across a truly outlandish but plausible rarepair lies in imagining how they’d interact, what they’d draw out in each other, what parallels and contrasts emerge, and how they might make you see familiar characters in a completely new light. At their best, crack-ships are simply play. They let fans explore hidden corners of canon and stretch the boundaries of character and chemistry. But they also raise a question: are we, in pairing the unpairable, really just seeking connection? Is it an attempt at trying to know others, and be known in return, through the act of imaginative projection? Or is it simply harmless escapism, a whimsical way to entertain unlikely what-ifs without consequence? Whatever the case, one thing’s certain: we’d love to see how Rachel McAdams and Devon Bostick would react to the ship. But the jury’s already out and the verdict is unanimous: we love it. Pictures / Moviestore Collection Ltd / Alamy) Netflix kicked off November by adding more than 40 movies to its library , and while there are several picks in the mix that deserve a spot in your watchlist, one that really stands out to me is “Game Night.” This 2018 action-comedy is a supremely enjoyable effort in the genre, and even though I’ve watched it more than once before, its arrival on Netflix has me itching to stream it all over again. “Game Night” boasts a strong comedic cast, including Jason Bateman, Rachel McAdams, Lamorne Morris and Jesse Plemons, all working from a sharp script that combines excellent gags and a narrative that spins off the rails in the best way. It's an easy recommendation if you’re looking for something entertaining to watch on Netflix this week. What is ‘Game Night’ about? GAME NIGHT - Official Trailer - YouTube Watch On Married couple Max (Jason Bateman) and Annie (Rachel McAdams) are board game and trivia enthusiasts who host a weekly game night with their friends. However, when Max's egotistical older brother, Brook (Kyle Chandler), offers to host the next evening, things are kicked up a notch when he plans an elaborate murder mystery for the friend group to solve. Pictures / Prod DB / Aggregate Films / Davis Entertainment / New Line Cinema / Alamy) “Game Night” has plenty of strengths, but its twisting plot is something that I certainly didn’t expect from a comedy of this nature. The dramatic irony of its lead thinking they’re playing a fake murder mystery game while actually in the middle of a real-life criminal conspiracy is a fantastic setup for excitement, and to keep things spicy, there are several enjoyable reveals. I believe that the best comedy movies should be quotable, and this is an area where “Game Night” certainly pulls a high score. There’s a reason that an early scene, where Jesse Plemons’ Gary, an aloof neighbor never invited to game night, is pondering how a three-for-one chip deal can be profitable for Frito-Lay, seems to go viral every other week. Plus, McAdam’s initial delight and then shock when a goon gets sucked into an airplane jet (“Oh no, he died!”) still makes me crack up even when I’m well aware it’s coming. Pictures / Prod DB / Aggregate Films / Davis Entertainment / New Line Cinema / Alamy ) While “Game Night” puts its best foot forward as a comedy, there are a few neat action moments as well. A creatively staged scene where the characters throw around a valuable item like a football to avoid it falling into the hands of goons is a real highlight. It’s not the only example of creative filmmaking from directors John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein, either. Despite the popularity of her character, Regina George, McAdams has declined opportunities to reprise the role. She believes the timing and conditions must be right for such a return. Rachel McAdams on Declining to Reprise Regina George McAdams gained fame in the early 2000s, particularly for her portrayal of Regina George in the teen classic Mean Girls. This character, the queen bee of the Plastics, became a pop culture phenomenon. Despite this, McAdams is not keen on revisiting her past roles for commercial projects. Why McAdams Is Not Interested Fans of Mean Girls may be disappointed to learn that McAdams is not interested in bringing back Regina George unless the opportunity aligns with her artistic vision. McAdams values her versatility as an actress. She prioritizes new projects over performing in commercials. Her absence during recent cast reunions, such as the Walmart advertisement, was not due to any personal conflicts with co-stars. While co-stars Lindsay Lohan, Lacey Chabert, and Amanda Seyfried participated in the advertisement, McAdams chose to step back. She expressed discomfort with the concept of reprising her character for an advertisement, fearing it might diminish her status in Hollywood. Future Opportunities In a recent interview with Variety, she shared her thoughts on the matter. “I wasn’t that excited about doing a commercial,” McAdams explained. However, she’s open to returning for a legitimate film project. “I would, of course, always love to be part of a Mean Girls reunion and hang with my Plastics,” she added. While current interest in a Mean Girls movie musical exists, McAdams has not confirmed her participation. By Jaja Agpalo @https://x.com/dzazing Published 03 November 2025, 9:53 PM GMT Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share on Reddit Share on Flipboard Share on Pocket Siebbi, CC BY 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons Some roles define an actor's career through box office success. Others gain power over time, simmering for years before emerging as a cultural touchstone. It is a fate reserved for films that capture a truth, often one that society is not quite ready for at the time. For Diane Lane, her 1982 film Ladies and Gentlemen, The Fabulous Stains falls squarely in the latter category. Nearly 45 years after she starred as a teenage punk, the actress is reflecting on the film's unexpected and powerful legacy. Speaking recently with Deadline , the three-time Golden Globe nominee expressed her pride. She feels 'very vindicated' that the film found its audience, even if it took decades. The movie, directed by Lou Adler, is now widely credited as a major influence on the 'riot grrrl' punk movement of the 1990s. This feminist music scene, which championed female empowerment and tackled difficult subjects, was defined by its aggressive, unapologetic politics. For many, The Fabulous Stains provided an early blueprint. 'It was so wild,' she said of the filming experience. 'It was airing not too long ago on TCM , and I was very vindicated to see that that film had the legs that it deserves to have, and it was wonderful to have been appreciated by people who went on in their music careers and were emboldened by our story.' How Diane Lane Captured a Punk Moment in Time Lane emphasized just how authentic the film's timing was. The sense of raw energy seen on screen was not manufactured; it was a snapshot of a cultural shift that defined the end of one decade and the start of another. 'It was February of 1980 when we filmed that. So, just put that in your pipe and smoke it. I mean, it was very real to the times just coming out of the 70s. So, punk was already there and getting only more so,' Lane continued. 'But as a point in history, it's lovely to say I was a part of it in whatever little way that I could be as a 15-year old girl in the film industry.' Diane Lane on the Film's Lasting 'Riot Grrrl' Legacy In Ladies and Gentlemen, The Fabulous Stains , Lane played the frustrated teen Corinne Burns. She forms a band, The Stains, with her sister Tracy (Marin Kanter) and their cousin Jessica McNeil, who was played by a very young Laura Dern. The film follows their journey as the trio joins a tour with a veteran punk group, The Looters, and navigates a swift, chaotic rise to global stardom. Adding to the film's gritty authenticity, the cast included real-life punk royalty. Members of the Sex Pistols, specifically Paul Thomas Cook and Steve Jones, were featured. Paul Simonon of The Clash also appeared. This integration of real musicians helped cement the film's status among punk fans who recognised the genuine article. Though The Fabulous Stains was not a commercial hit upon its release, it quickly garnered a cult following. Its influence has been cited by major figures in music. Icons such as Courtney Love, Bikini Kill's Tobi Vail, and Bratmobile's Allison Wolfe have all credited the film as a key inspiration for their own work, securing its place in punk history, long after its quiet initial release. Bassyonni 26 Nov 2025 Home News Sports Entertainment Tech Business Home News Diane Lane Celebrates Her Iconic Role in Punk History with ‘Fabulous Stains’ News Diane Lane Celebrates Her Iconic Role in Punk History with ‘Fabulous Stains’ Bassyonni ago 23 days Diane Lane recently expressed her pride in her role in the 1982 cult classic, *Ladies and Gentlemen, The Fabulous Stains*. This film has left a lasting impact on the punk music scene and is often seen as a precursor to the riot grrrl movement of the 1990s. Diane Lane Reflects on Her Punk Legacy In an interview with Deadline, Lane, a three-time Golden Globe nominee, reminisced about her experience filming the movie. Directed by Lou Adler, the film showcases the journey of Corinne Burns, a girl who forms a punk band with her sister and cousin. The movie was shot in February 1980, during a pivotal time for punk culture. Impact of the Film Lane highlighted the film’s relevance to its era, saying, “It was very real to the times just coming out of the 70s.” She noted that punk was burgeoning, making her involvement at such a young age—15 years old—meaningful. Lane felt vindicated upon seeing the continued appreciation for the film when it aired recently on TCM. Plot Overview In *Ladies and Gentlemen, The Fabulous Stains*, Lane’s character, Corinne, along with her sister Tracy (played by Marin Kanter) and cousin Jessica (portrayed by Laura Dern), forms a band called The Stains. Their journey begins when they tour with the punk band The Looters, quickly achieving fame. Cultural Significance The film has inspired numerous musicians, including Courtney Love and members of bands like Bikini Kill and Bratmobile. The cast includes notable figures such as Paul Thomas Cook and Steve Jones from the Sex Pistols, along with Paul Simonon from The Clash. Lane acknowledges the film’s historical position in the evolution of punk music. Overall, Diane Lane’s reflections on *Ladies and Gentlemen, The Fabulous Stains* underline the film’s significance in shaping punk history and its enduring influence on future generations of musicians. ANNIVERSARY: 3 ½ STARS. “creates a pressure-cooker of tension and menace.” « Richard Crouse Facebook Twitter Richard Crouse Bookography Biography ANNIVERSARY: 3 ½ STARS. “creates a pressure-cooker of tension and menace.” SYNOPSIS : In “Anniversary,” a new thriller now playing in theatres, Diane Lane and Kyle Chandler play Ellen and Paul, a liberal Georgetown University academic and chef celebrating twenty-five years of marriage. When Liz (Phoebe Dynevor), their son Josh’s (Dylan O’Brien) new girlfriend, writes a political screed titled “The Change: The New Social Contract,” its success sows the seeds of discontent within the family and the country. CAST : Diane Lane, Kyle Chandler, Madeline Brewer, Zoey Deutch, Phoebe Dynevor, Mckenna Grace, Daryl McCormack, and Dylan O’Brien. Directed by Jan Komasa. REVIEW : One of the least subtle films of the year, “Anniversary” dives headfirst into a maelstrom of ideological extremism, buried secrets and societal polarization. Featuring a large ensemble cast of veterans and newcomers, “Anniversary” begins at a lavish 25 th anniversary celebration for Ellen and Paul (Diane Lane and Kyle Chandler). Son Josh’s (Dylan O’Brien) date is Liz (Phoebe Dynevor), a former student of Ellen’s, kicked out of school after Ellen denounced her radical views. She’s now the author of “The Change: The New Social Contract,” a political diatribe supporting the implication of a “no-party” system that aims to “put the ‘united’ back in these states of America.” As the book becomes a national best-seller Ellen can’t hide her disapproval with its ideas of a singular, unified national belief system. “The book is a weapon,” she says amid her growing concerns for the fate of democracy as a spawning movement known as The Change, endorse pledging an oath to an alternate American flag. Liz’s newfound popularity during the rise of The Change—“The greatest movement in the history of this nation.”—reveals fractures in Ellen and Paul’s family and in the country. “Everything around us is changing,” says daughter Birdie (Mckenna Grace). “Fear went mainstream. A study of radicalism, “Anniversary” delivers its message with the force of a knee to the groin. Director Jan Komasa, working from a screenplay by Lori Rosene-Gambino, keeps the telling of the cautionary tale taut, creating a pressure-cooker of tension and menace. The ideological conflict between the family—the “Non-Changers”—and The Change escalates quickly, but Komasa smartly keeps the focus on the individuals and the radical transformations in their lives. “You have obliterated us,” Ellen says to Liz. “What more do you want?” O’Brien is chilling as he navigates Josh’s transformation from failed writer to intimidating demagogue. A contentious scene between Josh and Paul allows O’Brien and Chandler to explore the boundaries of the polarization that has gripped the family in a powerful fashion. That edgy conflict drips with ice, but it is the helplessness Ellen and Paul, once a couple living their best lives, feels as their existence is completely upended by The Change that resonates. “You need to decide,” a census taker tells them, “whether you’re with us for against us.” “Anniversary” is a provocative, timely drama that swings for the fences, and while the portrait it paints of extremism is vivid, and in many ways uncompromising, it is the personal toll of the characters that unnerves. In an interview with Deadline, the 3x Golden Globe nominee recently reflected on her Lou Adler-directed 1982 cult classic Ladies and Gentlemen, The Fabulous Stains , which is largely credited for influencing the riot grrrl movement of the ’90s. “It was so wild,” she said of filming the movie as a teen. “It was airing not too long ago on TCM, and I was very vindicated to see that that film had the legs that it deserves to have, and it was wonderful to have been appreciated by people who went on in their music careers and were emboldened by our story.” Related Stories News Diane Lane & ‘Anniversary’ Co-Stars Reacted To “The Experiment That Is Democracy” Over Group Text After Wrap Festivals ‘Modi – Three Days On The Wing Of Madness’ Review: Punk Rock Lives In Johnny Depp’s Riotous Celebration Of Artistic Excess – San Sebastian Lane continued, “It was February of 1980 when we filmed that. So, just put that in your pipe and smoke it. I mean, it was very real to the times just coming out of the 70s. So, punk was already there and getting only more so. But as a point in history, it’s lovely to say I was a part of it in whatever little way that I could be as a 15-year old girl in the film industry.” In Ladies and Gentlemen, The Fabulous Stains , Lane starred as frustrated teen Corinne Burns, who forms the band, The Stains, with her sister Tracy (Marin Kanter) and their cousin Jessica McNeil (Laura Dern). When the punk group, The Looters, comes to town, the trio joins their tour and quickly rises to global stardom. The cast also featured the Sex Pistols’ Paul Thomas Cook and Steve Jones, as well as The Clash’s Paul Simonon. New York City mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani (D.) has presented himself as a voice for the working class, but a new report states that he has worked with an A-list stylist who has managed the images of Democratic elites and celebrities. Mamdani and his wife, Rama Duwaji, have received advice from stylist Bailey Moon, Puck reported Thursday. Moon is perhaps best known for his work as a "wardrobe adviser" to former president Joe Biden and former first lady Jill Biden, a task that the stylist called "the honor of a lifetime." He also styled former Hillary Clinton aide Huma Abedin for her wedding to left-wing billionaire heir Alex Soros, whose progressive empire pumped tens of millions of dollars into groups backing Mamdani's candidacy. Moon has worked with less sartorially inclined Democrats before, including Minnesota governor Tim Walz during Walz's time as former vice president Kamala Harris's 2024 running mate. Other celebrity clients Moon has styled include Pamela Anderson, Diane Lane, Rebecca Hall, Morgan Spector, and Zachary Quinto. News of Mamdani's consultations with a stylist comes just two days after a speech in which the future mayor credited working-class New Yorkers with his win. Exit polls, on the other hand, show that it was the city's most educated elite who lifted Mamdani to victory and that those without bachelor's or advanced degrees preferred former governor Andrew Cuomo (D). Moon, for his part, told the New York Post on Thursday that Mamdani did not pay him for his advice. The stylist has worked with a wide variety of clients but has said there is one category of person he will not assist. "I would not work with the Trump administration," he told Vogue in January. "The values do have to be there, and I don't align with Republican values." Let’s not talk politics, Paul (Kyle Chandler) repeatedly urges his family on a series of get-togethers. At the first, celebrating the 25th wedding anniversary of Paul, a restauranteur, and Ellen (Diane Lane), an academic at Georgetown, it scarcely matters, may even literally go without saying. The couple’s four children converge upon their childhood home, and any unease or sniping seems purely familial. But for Liz (Phoebe Dynevor), an outsider, there’s more going on. She’s newly engaged to Paul and Ellen’s only son Josh (Dylan O’Brien), an as-yet-unsuccessful writer, though it turns out she also took a class with Ellen at Georgetown. There are small-p political undertones to Josh’s interest in Liz, too: They met through a shared agent, and he’s helped her with a book project that seems much further along than the sci-fi novels he’s about to abandon. Anniversary lets this information out gradually, with intentional awkwardness, as it introduces these characters as well as daughters Anna (Madeline Brewer), a firebrand stand-up comic; Cynthia (Zoey Deutch), an environmental lawyer alongside her partner Rob (Daryl McCormack); and youngest Birdie (Mckenna Grace), an introverted teenage science prodigy. Liz, who Dynevor plays with a wounded, self-conscious poise perfectly suiting her suppressed English accent, finds it difficult to gain social footing with the family, though they’re not altogether unwelcoming. But you also get the sense she knew, going in, that this would be a struggle. She has other plans. The movie is largely about those broader plans coming to fruition through the publication of Liz’s book The Change: A New Social Compact , which kicks off a movement disguising single-party authoritarianism as third-option humanism. There are certain conceits Anniversary asks the audience to accept, and perhaps the most difficult is the idea that a lengthy nonfiction book becomes a galvanizing force for social change in the 21st century. It’s logistically cleaner than setting up Liz as an influencer or a podcaster, and the loftier packaging of her ideas strikes more directly at the intellectual reputation of her eventual mother-in-law, but also: come on. If there’s something the movie gets particularly wrong, it’s the degree of whitewashing it imagines fascism requiring in the United States, maybe because its right-wing revolution was conceived and shot during a brief four-year pause in the real-life version. The movie also indulges some retrograde ideas about who would be persecuted first and most thoroughly in this situation – namely, “truth-telling” comedians like Anna; neither her rise nor fall scan as especially believable, because she’s an academic’s idea of a comic (which also means the movie misses any opportunity for more contemporary critique of what counts as free speech in comedy and what doesn’t). What Jan Komasa’s film gets right is how so much right-wing radicalization, especially in upper classes, stems from status-based grievances. As it surveys a five-year period through a series of increasingly grim family gatherings – Thanksgiving, with the obligatory no-politics-at-the-dinner-table warning; a birthday; another anniversary party – Josh clearly relishes the opportunity to go from mild failson (at least compared to two of his successful sisters) to coattail-riding thought leader. O’Brien is a cast stand-out as he radiates serenely toxic smugness, becoming one of the year’s most chilling on-screen villains without ever raising his voice. Dynevor’s Liz, too, is essentially out for well-heeled, primly spoken revenge in the form of national unity. Though the cast is large, Komasa and screenwriter Lori Rosene-Gambino juggle a variety of reactions to the rise of fascism, from numb despondence to fiery resistance to Paul’s no-politics capitulation. It’s especially gratifying to see Lane given such a dramatically substantial lead role. So why is it easier to regard Annivesary with interest and some admiration than to wholeheartedly recommend it? I think it’s because the shape of the material repeatedly cries out for a different medium entirely. There are countless dialogue scenes that are easy to picture translating perfectly to a stage setting, and if some of the performances lose the additional nuance of Komasa’s close-ups, the electricity of live, real-time confrontations would likely more than compensate. (Plus, it wouldn’t require looking at the dreary washed-out digital-indie look of this film, which is probably appropriate but does the actors no favors.) A novel, on the other hand, could grant characters like Anna, Cynthia, and Birdie an interiority that a packed ensemble film doesn’t have room for. The movie, on the other hand, allows our eyes and minds to drift towards the limits of the frame, turning the family home set into a distraction, rather than an effective dramatic tool. A play or a novel could make better use of those empty spaces. Still, I understand why Komasa wanted this to be a film (and not just because he’s a filmmaker). After all, who reads these days? Podcasts The Ocean is a Killer in 2000’s ‘The Perfect Storm’ [Murder Made Fiction Podcast] Published 2 weeks ago on November 10, 2025 By Joe Lipsett After spending the entirety of October tackling Ed Gein titles such as Monster: The Ed Gein Story , as well as Deranged and In The Light of the Moon , as well as Peacock’s limited Devil in Disguise: John Wayne Gacy series, Jenn and I needed a break from human serial killers. For November, we’re turning our attention to Aquatic Disasters: real life cases of peril and human adversity out on the dangerous open water. First up: Wolfgang Peterson ‘s 2000 spectacle The Perfect Storm , featuring an all-star cast that includes George Clooney , Mark Wahlberg , John C Reilly , William Fichtner , John Hawkes , and Diane Lane . The film, which was written by William D. Wittliff and adapted from Sebastian Junger ‘s non-fiction book of the same name, follows the crew of the swordfish fishing vessel Andrea Gail. In 1991, Captain Billy Tyne (Clooney) and his five man crew ventured far off the coast of Newfoundland in search of a late season catch and got caught in what meteorologist Todd Gross ( Christopher McDonald ) described as “The Perfect Storm.” The film depicts their epic struggle to survive, the women they left behind, including Lane’s Chris, and several others caught in the storm. This includes a trio aboard a sailboat, as well as the Air National Guard helicopter crew dispatched to pull survivors out of the water. At a certain point, the film segues into fiction territory because we’ll never know what exactly happened aboard the Andrea Gail after they broke off contact with the Captain of Hannah Boden , Linda Greenlaw ( Mary Elizabeth Mastrantonio ), though the bodies of the men were never recovered. Despite being a tragedy, The Perfect Storm is also a quintessential summer action spectacle, as well as an ode to blue collar workers, and a dazzling special effects feast that still holds up twenty-five years later. Does James Horner ‘s score go way too hard for way too long in order to make audiences feel something? Yes, but despite this, The Perfect Storm remains a pretty entertaining piece of “based on a true story” fiction. If you want even more Murder Made Fiction , be sure to check out the pod’s Patreon feed for ~110 hours of bonus content, including episode by episode coverage of November titles such as Netflix’s The Monster of Florence and Hulu’s ripped-from-the-headlines limited series, Murdaugh: Murder in the Family starring Jason Clarke and Patricia Arquette. Thomas Howell, Patrick Swayze and Matt Dillon, according to The Hollywood Reporter. The Outsiders, based on author S. E. Hinton's book of the same name, was set in Tulsa, Oklahoma, in 1964. Lane also recalled one memorable moment while shooting for the film, the drive-in cinema scene with Howell, who played Ponyboy Curtis. "I remember when we were at the movie theatre and they were creating this windstorm.
